hero.headline: Old Havana Cafe and House of Hope build 400-foot Cuban sandwich in Palm City, break world record
hero.teaser: A 400-foot Cuban sandwich built Saturday morning in Palm City set a new world record and raised more than $30,000 for House of Hope.
hero.body:
Old Havana Cafe and House of Hope built a 400-foot Cuban sandwich Saturday morning in Palm City, breaking the previous world record held by Tampa. The event raised more than $30,000 for House of Hope, a Martin County nonprofit that provides food assistance, job training, education and other services aimed at helping local families become more self-sufficient.

A large crowd turned out to watch volunteers and sandwich builders assemble the record-breaking Cuban sandwich. Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi completed the final measurement confirming the sandwich reached 400 feet.

Organizers said the event was about more than setting a world record. It was also designed to bring the community together while raising awareness and support for House of Hope's mission.

cards.headline: Martin County High School bomb threat traced to Russia, sheriff's office says
cards.body:
A bomb threat at Martin County High School prompted the evacuation of students and staff Thursday afternoon, with investigators now suspecting the threat originated from Russia, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

The threat was sent via email Thursday afternoon, leading to an immediate response from law enforcement. The Martin County School District notified families that there was an increased law enforcement presence on campus in response to the emailed bomb threat. All students and staff were evacuated away from campus buildings while authorities conducted their investigation.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office conducted a comprehensive search of the property Thursday afternoon. After completing the search, law enforcement determined that no threat actually existed. The district confirmed later Thursday that no evidence of a threat was found.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed on Friday that they are investigating the incident and suspect the threat originated out of Russia. The sheriff's office continues to investigate the hoax threat.

hero.headline: Indian River County school bus driver arrested on child abuse charge
hero.teaser: A Sebastian woman who worked as a school bus driver for the School District of Indian River County was arrested Thursday on a child abuse charge after surveillance footage allegedly showed her injuring and threatening a student.
hero.body:
A school bus driver in Indian River County has been arrested on a child abuse charge following an investigation into an incident involving a student on a school bus, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies said Tracy Marie Alpy, 65, of Sebastian, was arrested Thursday and charged with one count of child abuse. Jail records show she was being held without bond. Alpy worked as a bus driver for the School District of Indian River County.

According to an arrest affidavit, investigators reviewed school bus surveillance video related to an incident that reportedly happened Aug. 24 while Alpy was working as a bus driver. The footage showed an interaction between Alpy and a student that led to the criminal investigation. Investigators wrote that the video appeared to show Alpy removing the child from a seat, grabbing the student and bending the child's finger. Deputies said Alpy could also be heard making a threatening remark toward the student during the encounter.

The child later told investigators they were frightened by what happened, according to the report. Deputies said they determined there was probable cause to arrest Alpy on a charge of child abuse. Alpy declined to speak with investigators without an attorney present, the affidavit states.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after 8 explosive devices found at home on Balsam Drive
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man is in custody after St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office detectives discovered eight suspected explosive devices at his home while serving a risk protection order Thursday.

Detectives identified suspected destructive devices at a residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive around 12:20 p.m. Thursday, prompting a street closure that lasted roughly 10 to 14 hours as investigators removed the explosives. Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives — possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices.

Morrone allowed deputies to search his home and car to retrieve weapons and ammunition in accordance with the risk protection order. During that search, detectives saw what appeared to be military-style hand grenades inside the house. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team responded and safely removed seven devices appearing to be replica hand grenades that had been modified. Morrone admitted to tampering with them, according to his arrest report.

After obtaining a search warrant, investigators found an additional improvised explosive device, bringing the total to eight. The sheriff's office said investigators also located a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were taken from the home related to the risk protection order. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the investigation underscores the seriousness of what detectives encountered. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices," Del Toro said.

According to court records, a judge granted the risk protection order after finding reasonable cause to believe Morrone posed a significant danger to himself or others. The document states Morrone had recently been involved in an act or threat of violence and had recently used or threatened to use a weapon. The order required Morrone to surrender his firearms and ammunition immediately.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on eight explosive-device charges after IEDs found at Balsam Drive home
hero.teaser: Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, faces eight counts after St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office detectives serving a risk protection order Thursday found eight improvised explosive devices and bomb-making materials at his residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive.
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man Friday on eight counts of explosives, possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices after detectives serving a risk protection order discovered improvised explosive devices at his home. Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, was arrested and charged following the investigation that began Thursday at his residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. He is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

Detectives with the SLCSO Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the residence at approximately 12:20 p.m. Thursday when they identified suspected destructive devices, Fort Pierce police said in a news release Friday morning. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team. Bomb technicians conducted a preliminary examination of the suspected devices and removed seven devices from the residence, safely securing them in a containment vessel.

Detectives subsequently obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the execution of the search warrant, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. This brought the total number of improvised explosive devices recovered from the residence to eight. Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of a risk protection order.

"This investigation underscores the seriousness of what our detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to the threats around us," Sheriff Richard Del Toro said. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices. I'm proud of their professionalism and courage, and grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as we continue this investigation." The investigation remains ongoing, and there is no immediate threat to the community.

Neighbors expressed concern about the situation. "That's really bad," Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, told WPBF. Rates described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," he said.

hero.headline: Palm City event raises $30,000 for House of Hope with 400-foot world-record Cuban sandwich
hero.teaser: Old Havana Cafe and House of Hope built a 400-foot Cuban sandwich in Palm City on Saturday, breaking the previous world record and raising more than $30,000 for the local nonprofit.
hero.body:
Old Havana Cafe and House of Hope built a 400-foot Cuban sandwich in Palm City on Saturday morning, breaking the previous world record and raising more than $30,000 for the Martin County nonprofit. The event raised funds for House of Hope, which provides food assistance, job training, education and other services aimed at helping local families become more self-sufficient.

The massive sandwich broke the previous world record held by Tampa. A large crowd turned out to watch volunteers and sandwich builders assemble the record-breaking Cuban sandwich and support the fundraiser.

Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi was on hand to complete the final measurement confirming the sandwich reached 400 feet.

Organizers said the event was about more than setting a world record. It was also designed to bring the community together while raising awareness and support for House of Hope's mission.

cards.headline: Martin County bomb threat believed to have originated from Russia, sheriff says
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed Friday that investigators suspect the bomb threat that emptied Martin County High School originated from Russia.

Law enforcement evacuated students and staff from the campus Thursday afternoon after receiving the emailed threat. The sheriff's office conducted a comprehensive search of the property and determined no actual threat existed.

The Martin County School District notified families Thursday in an email that all students and staff had been evacuated away from campus buildings while law enforcement searched the property. The district reported an increased law enforcement presence on campus in response to the threat.

The district confirmed later Thursday that no evidence of a threat was found. The sheriff's office investigation into the origin of the threat continues.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after 8 explosive devices found at home on Balsam Drive
hero.body:
A Fort Pierce man is in custody after investigators found eight improvised explosive devices at his home while serving a risk protection order.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office began its investigation Thursday around 12:20 p.m. when detectives identified suspected destructive devices at a residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, allowed deputies to search his home and car to retrieve weapons and ammunition in accordance with the order. During that search, detectives saw what appeared to be military-style hand grenades inside the house.

Deputies say seven devices appearing to be replica hand grenades were modified, and Morrone admitted to tampering with them. The sheriff's office Bomb Disposal Team safely removed the seven devices from the residence. After obtaining a search warrant, investigators found an additional improvised explosive device, bringing the total to eight. Investigators also located a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Investigators have not said whether any of the devices are functional.

Neighbors said the street was closed for roughly 10 to 14 hours Thursday as investigators removed the explosives from the home. Morrone's son, who was loading a truck with ammunition from inside the home, said he does not believe his father was planning to use the devices to harm anyone.

Morrone was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives — possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices. Eight firearms were also taken from the home related to the risk protection order. He is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

According to court records, a judge granted the risk protection order after finding reasonable cause to believe Morrone posed a significant danger to himself or others. The document states Morrone had recently been involved in an act or threat of violence and had recently used or threatened to use a weapon. The order required Morrone to surrender his firearms and ammunition immediately.

"This investigation underscores the seriousness of what our detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to the threats around us," said Sheriff Richard Del Toro. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices."

hero.headline: Martin County leaders call for return to post-9/11 unity at Palm City bridge walk
hero.teaser: County leaders and residents crossed Veterans Memorial Bridge in Palm City on Friday carrying photographs of attack victims as speakers urged a return to the cooperation felt immediately after Sept. 11, 2001.
hero.body:
Martin County leaders and residents marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks Friday morning with a memorial bridge walk in Palm City, where speakers called for a return to the unity Americans experienced in the days after the attacks.

The annual event at Jock Leighton Park near Veterans Memorial Bridge honored the nearly 3,000 people killed during the terrorist attacks. Participants crossed Veterans Memorial Bridge carrying photographs representing nearly every person who died during the attacks on the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and aboard hijacked airplanes.

Martin County Commission Chair Sarah Heard said the country responded with "unity, civility, respect, cooperation, generosity" following the attacks. "We were the United States. This is what I choose to remember," Heard said. Several leaders throughout the ceremony referenced Sept. 12, 2001, describing it as a moment when Americans came together despite political and personal differences. Commissioner Stacey Hetherington also reflected on the sense of togetherness Americans experienced after the attacks. "September 12th is also remembered because we united, we came together and we worked in unity," Hetherington said.

Community volunteer Mayce DelValle, who helped organize the memorial walk, said many people at Friday's ceremony expressed a longing to see that spirit return. "September 12th was a big day," DelValle said. "That was the day that the world actually came together in unity — neighbors hugging neighbors, friends helping friends, strangers embracing strangers. That's what we need to focus on. That is how we can truly honor those that perished." DelValle also carried photographs honoring Mark Zepplin and Kevin Marlowe, people she personally knew who died in the Twin Towers. "These guys were like family to me," DelValle said. "They unfortunately lost their lives in the buildings at the Twin Towers at Ground Zero on that day."

Martin County Fire Rescue Chief Chad Cianciulli described the patriotism that emerged immediately following the attacks. Chaplain Hoss Wiggins led a prayer before participants began the memorial walk, saying "After that awful event, the next day, a nation united in prayer."

Chaplain Hoss Wiggins continued the theme during a prayer delivered before participants began the memorial walk. “After that awful event, the next day, a nation united in prayer,” Wiggins said. “They set aside their differences and they united, and they cried out to God Almighty for help.” Wiggins said memorial events taking place across the country serve as reminders not to forget the sacrifices made by victims, first responders and military members. “The word of God encourages us over and over and over again to remember or don’t forget,” Wiggins said. “And that’s what we’re here today to do is to remember those who paid the ultimate sacrifice.” Before leading the crowd in prayer, Wiggins energized participants with a phrase familiar to many firefighters gathered at the event. “What I mean by ‘let the big dog eat,’ you simply focus on the task at hand,” Wiggins said before encouraging the crowd to respond together. Wiggins then prayed for the protection of first responders, local communities and the nation. Every American chose unity, civility, respect, cooperation, generosity. New York City was unrecognizable, buried in widespread rubble. cards.headline: Bomb threat email forced evacuation at Martin County High School; FBI involved
cards.body:
A bomb threat email sent Thursday afternoon forced the evacuation of Martin County High School and triggered a multi-agency investigation now involving the FBI. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the email threatened three bombs on campus and claimed they would detonate by 2:30 p.m. or 3 p.m.

Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. Budensiek said the person living at that address appears to be a victim whose account was hacked from Russia. The sheriff said the incident may be linked to a broader pattern of swatting cases.

"The individual that we're dealing with in the city of Stuart appears at that time to be victimized himself. His account looks like it was hacked from Russia, and then this email from Russia, so this is a trend we've seen over and over again," Budensiek said. He added that the person named in the email is from Ukraine.

Deputies went to the Stuart residence, and Budensiek said the person has been cooperative. Investigators are conducting forensics to confirm the account was hacked and the email originated from Russia. The Martin County Sheriff's Office contacted the FBI tip line as part of the investigation.

The school was evacuated and parents were notified. Deputies swept the campus and found no credible threat. The school day resumed after the all-clear. Budensiek said public safety is his top priority.

I planted three bombs (gave the location) and don't waste your time looking for them because they're going to go off by 3 o'clock or 2:30 p.m.,'" Budensiek said. Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. But we've got to check the boxes, go through the forensics side of it, and make sure that that email was indeed hacked. It did indeed come from Russia; we can see that part at this point, but we've got some things to vet out. Our person in that email is ironically from Ukraine," Budensiek said. hero.headline: Martin County High School evacuated after bomb threat email traced to hacked Stuart account
hero.body:
Martin County High School was evacuated Thursday afternoon after an email threatened a bomb attack at the campus. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, school district, and FBI tip line responded to the threat. Deputies conducted a sweep and determined there was no credible threat. The school day resumed after the all-clear.

Sheriff John Budensiek said the email claimed the sender planted three bombs at the school and warned they would detonate by 2:30 p.m. or 3 p.m. Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. The Stuart resident appears to be a victim whose account was hacked from Russia, according to Budensiek.

Budensiek said the incident may be linked to other swatting cases. Deputies were at the Stuart home, and the resident cooperated with investigators. The sheriff said investigators must verify through forensics that the email was hacked and came from Russia. Budensiek said the person named in the email is from Ukraine.

Parents were notified during the evacuation. Budensiek emphasized that public safety is his top priority. The investigation continues as authorities work to confirm the details of the hacked account and explore possible connections to a broader pattern of swatting incidents.
hero.article_text: An email threatening a bomb attack at Martin County High School on Thursday afternoon led to an evacuation and a law enforcement response involving the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the school district, and the FBI's tip line. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the email raised concerns. "And the email says, 'I'm this male (not going to name him). I hate this school (Martin County High School). I planted three bombs (gave the location) and don't waste your time looking for them because they're going to go off by 3 o'clock or 2:30 p.m.,'" Budensiek said. Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "The individual that we're dealing with in the city of Stuart appears at that time to be victimized himself. His account looks like it was hacked from Russia, and then this email from Russia, so this is a trend we've seen over and over again," Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident may be linked to other swatting cases. "We are at the individual's home; they've been cooperative so far. But we've got to check the boxes, go through the forensics side of it, and make sure that that email was indeed hacked. It did indeed come from Russia; we can see that part at this point, but we've got some things to vet out. Our person in that email is ironically from Ukraine," Budensiek said. The school was evacuated, parents were notified, and deputies conducted a sweep of the campus. After determining there was no credible threat, the school day resumed. hero.body:
A 57-year-old Fort Pierce man was arrested Thursday after deputies serving a risk protection order at his home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive discovered eight improvised explosive devices, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Court records show a judge had granted the risk protection order after finding reasonable cause to believe Keith Anthony Morrone posed a significant danger to himself or others.

The investigation began around 12:20 p.m. Thursday when detectives identified suspected destructive devices at the residence. Morrone allowed deputies to search his home and car to retrieve weapons and ammunition in accordance with the order. During that search, detectives saw what appeared to be military-style hand grenades inside the house, prompting the sheriff's bomb squad to respond.

Deputies say seven devices appearing to be replica hand grenades were modified, and investigators say Morrone admitted to tampering with them. After obtaining a search warrant, investigators found an additional improvised explosive device, bringing the total to eight. The sheriff's office said investigators also located a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Bomb technicians safely removed all devices from the residence. Investigators have not said whether any of the devices are functional.

Neighbors said the street was closed for roughly 10 to 14 hours Thursday as investigators removed the explosives from the home. Morrone was charged with eight counts of explosives, possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices. Eight firearms were also taken from the home related to the risk protection order. The court document states Morrone had recently been involved in an act or threat of violence and had recently used or threatened to use a weapon. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action. The investigation remains ongoing.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man charged with eight counts after bomb squad removes explosive devices from Balsam Drive home
hero.body:
Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was formally charged with eight counts of possessing, making or attempting to make a destructive device after the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team removed eight suspected explosive devices and explosive-making materials from his Balsam Drive home. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

Detectives with the sheriff's office Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the home at about 12:20 p.m. Thursday when they identified numerous suspected destructive devices. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area while requesting assistance from the Bomb Disposal Team.

Bomb technicians removed seven suspected destructive devices from the home and placed them in a containment vessel. After obtaining a search warrant, deputies found and safely removed an eighth suspected explosive device, along with a large quantity of materials used to make explosive devices. Eight firearms were also seized from the home as part of the risk protection order.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the sheriff's office is working with the FBI and ATF as the investigation continues. The sheriff's office said there is no immediate threat to the community.

"This investigation underscores the seriousness of what our detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to the threats around us," Del Toro said. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices. I'm proud of their professionalism and courage, and grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as we continue this investigation."

hero.headline: Two arrested in Indian River County for illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over Labor Day weekend
hero.body:
Indian River County deputies arrested two men in separate cases involving alleged illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over the Labor Day weekend, according to arrest affidavits.

Corey Michael Smith of Vero Beach was arrested Sept. 4 after deputies responded to a trespassing call at a BP gas station on 9th Street Southwest. A helicopter crew had spotted Smith on Indian River County School Board property near 800 20th Avenue. Deputies found him at the gas station with five black bags containing saw palmetto stalks.

Smith showed deputies a palmetto berry harvesting permit that listed an address on 17th Avenue Southwest. The property owner told deputies Smith did not have permission to harvest on the property, which belongs to the Salvation Army. Smith was arrested on charges of using a false or forged palmetto berry harvest permit, disclosing police radio information to aid a suspect, and trespassing after a warning. A deputy heard dispatch traffic coming from a scanner app on Smith's phone while he was detained, the affidavit states.

Francis Ostrowski was arrested a day later after a sheriff's office camera in the North County Conservation Area near 7800 130th Street captured a man carrying a bag filled with saw palmetto berries. Deputies located Ostrowski nearby with a bag of berries and asked whether he had a permit to harvest them. Ostrowski said he did not. He was arrested on a felony charge of harvesting an endangered plant without a permit.

The arrests come amid a series of recent saw palmetto berry cases across the Treasure Coast. CBS12 previously reported on arrests involving the alleged theft of about 200 pounds of berries in Martin County and about 150 pounds in Indian River County. In another recent case, a Boynton Beach man was arrested after deputies said they found about 500 pounds of saw palmetto berries.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after bomb squad recovers eight explosive devices from Balsam Drive home
hero.body:
Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was arrested Friday and charged with eight counts of possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices after the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team recovered improvised explosive devices and bomb-making materials from his home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

The investigation began Thursday at approximately 12:20 p.m. when detectives with the sheriff's office Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the residence and identified suspected destructive devices. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the Bomb Disposal Team. Bomb technicians conducted a preliminary examination and removed seven devices from the residence, safely securing them in a containment vessel.

Detectives subsequently obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the execution of the search warrant, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. This brought the total number of improvised explosive devices recovered from the residence to eight. Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of the risk protection order.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the investigation underscores the seriousness of what detectives encountered. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices," Del Toro said. "I'm proud of their professionalism and courage, and grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as we continue this investigation." The investigation remains ongoing, and there is no immediate threat to the community.

Neighbors expressed concern about the situation. Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," Rates said.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce honors 9/11 victims at Veterans Memorial Park ceremony
cards.teaser: The Treasure Coast community gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce for a 9/11 remembrance ceremony honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed and those impacted by the attacks. The ceremony included a wreath-laying for Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93.
cards.body:
The Treasure Coast community gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce for a 9/11 remembrance ceremony honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed, first responders, veterans, and others impacted by the attacks.

The ceremony included a wreath-laying to honor Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93, which crashed into a Pennsylvania field after passengers and crew fought back against the hijackers. Her final phone call to her husband deeply moved the crowd. "I hope to be able to see your face again, baby. I love you, bye," Lyles said in her last call.

Jerome Sangalli, a United Airlines International Purser AFA-CWA Boston and former union vice-president, described the emotional impact of hearing her words. "I held it together until I heard that phone call. I was just rushed back to when 9/11 happened," Sangalli said. He also expressed his admiration for the bravery of those aboard Flight 93. "All the flight attendants, all the pilots, they're all angels," Sangalli said.

Dennis McWilliams, who lost four family members on 9/11, shared how his family has used their tragic memories to strengthen their bond. "Our family has taken a stance to use those awful tragic memories at our family reunions, at our weddings, at our funerals to bring ourselves closer to one another," McWilliams said.

The ceremony also carried a message of unity, with local officials calling for the nation to recapture the sense of togetherness felt after the attacks. "I think we should use the memories of 9/11 to unite our country again, to remember those feelings of pride that we had in the immediate aftermath of such a tragic loss," McWilliams said.

"At the end of the day, we need to come back together as we did on that fateful day and months and years after. The United States has to come back together," Fort Pierce Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky said.

hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff links bomb threat at high school to Russia-based swatting scheme
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek confirmed Thursday that a bomb threat email which forced the evacuation of Martin County High School is linked to a broader swatting trend, with investigators tracing the hacked email account to Russia and a Ukrainian victim in Stuart.

The threatening email arrived Thursday afternoon, prompting an immediate evacuation and response from the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the school district, and the FBI's tip line. The email claimed the sender had planted three bombs at Martin County High School that would detonate by 2:30 p.m. or 3 p.m.

Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. The individual at that Stuart residence appears to be a victim whose account was hacked from Russia before the threatening email was sent. Budensiek said the person who lives at that Stuart address is from Ukraine and has been cooperative with investigators.

"The individual that we're dealing with in the city of Stuart appears at that time to be victimized himself. His account looks like it was hacked from Russia, and then this email from Russia, so this is a trend we've seen over and over again," Budensiek said.

Budensiek said the incident may be linked to other swatting cases. Investigators are conducting forensic analysis to confirm the email was hacked and originated from Russia.

Parents were notified of the threat and the school was evacuated. Deputies conducted a sweep of the campus. After determining there was no credible threat, the school day resumed.

"We are at the individual's home; they've been cooperative so far. But we've got to check the boxes, go through the forensics side of it, and make sure that that email was indeed hacked. It did indeed come from Russia; we can see that part at this point, but we've got some things to vet out. Our person in that email is ironically from Ukraine," Budensiek said.

The sheriff emphasized that public safety is his top priority.

hero.headline: Fellsmere approves The Point Surf Park, expecting $12M economic impact
hero.body:
Fellsmere has approved The Point Surf Park, a project city officials say is expected to bring about $12 million to the area and could help put the small community on the map.

The city worked closely with the developer to make the surf park a reality. Robert Loring, the city's community development director, said the approval followed a long and arduous journey.

Fellsmere has fewer than 5,000 residents, but city officials say the community has significant room for growth. Loring said in a statement that the park will generate new interest in the community and be a sincere benefit to residents.

"The city has so much potential and has been hidden from view for so many years, that finally people are just now noticing our lands and our surrounding amenities," Loring said. The surf park will feature adjustable waves that can be set to different heights.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport opens $3M renovation with dual baggage claim, covered walkways
hero.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed a $3 million renovation project that is now open to passengers, featuring dual baggage claim gates, covered walkways, and a new courtyard seating area. Airport officials said the upgrades were designed to improve the travel experience for passengers.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said the new terminal includes two baggage claim gates located about 100 feet from where aircraft park. The project also added canopies over passenger walkways and baggage claim areas, along with a courtyard where passengers can wait for their flights.

Passenger Austin Garafola said the improvements represent a substantial upgrade from previous conditions. "Oh, it's definitely a lot better than it was. You go right in right under the awning, and then everything is so much better. We used to have to wait in single file coming out; you get rained on, you get everything, but yeah, significantly better," Garafola said. Passenger Doris Newell called the facility great and praised the accessibility.

Airport officials announced plans for a concession area for departing passengers, and new long-term parking has been approved. The airport serves three commercial airlines: American, JetBlue and Breeze. Dambeck said the upgrades will create a better experience for passengers as they wait for their flights. Officials also plan to seek public input later this year on discussion about a possible new terminal.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce native CeeCee Lyles honored at Flight 93 Memorial on 25th anniversary of 9/11
cards.teaser: The family of CeeCee Ross Lyles, a Fort Pierce flight attendant who died on United Flight 93, gathered in Shanksville, Pennsylvania this week for the 25th anniversary ceremony at the Flight 93 Memorial.
cards.body:
The family of CeeCee Ross Lyles, a Fort Pierce flight attendant who died on United Flight 93, gathered in Shanksville, Pennsylvania this week for the 25th anniversary ceremony at the Flight 93 Memorial. Lyles and other passengers and crew fought back against hijackers on Sept. 11, 2001, forcing the plane to crash into a field in Pennsylvania and preventing it from reaching its intended target in Washington, D.C.

A statue stands in Lyles' honor on the shores of the Indian River Lagoon in Fort Pierce. Her husband said at the anniversary, "The 25th anniversary. I feel like every day or, well, almost every day, because her picture is all around the house. You know, I really miss her. She was such a beautiful woman."

Lyles grew up in Fort Pierce and served as a police officer and detective before pursuing her childhood dream of becoming a flight attendant. She had been in the role for just 10 months before Sept. 11. That day, 19 minutes into the hijacking, Lyles called her husband and left a message on their answering machine. "Baby, you have to listen to me carefully," she said. Calmly, she asked him to tell her sons, Jerome and Javon, that she loved them. Moments later, passengers and crew stormed the cockpit.

Today, Lyles' sons are parents themselves. "She would have three grandkids. She would have three for myself and three from Javon. So she would be arms full at the moment. Yes, she would," said Jerome. "Twenty-five years is … it's been a long time of missing her and, you know, wishing she was here with her family and kids and my kids and, you know, a lot of, a lot of moments, like a lot of, you know, cherished moments have been missed," he added.

Lyles' brother, Tony, said, "She was a good, good, good sister that cared about people. And I just miss her with all my heart and just glad to have been a part of her life for as long as I was." A family member said, "One good thing that came out of it was that the nation and all and everybody just came together in a spirit of unity, and that seemed to have lasted for a couple of months. And I pray that as we enter into this 25th year anniversary, that we can celebrate that spirit of unity."

Each year, the family awards scholarships in Lyles' name to graduating seniors, who must write an essay about her life to earn it. Some family members say the community they have found at the Shanksville memorial now feels like family of its own.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce ceremony honors 9/11 victims, hometown hero CeeCee Lyles
cards.teaser: Community members gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce to remember the nearly 3,000 people killed in the September 11 attacks and pay special tribute to Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93.
cards.body:
Community members gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce for a 9/11 remembrance ceremony honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed, first responders, veterans, and others impacted by the attacks.

The ceremony included a wreath-laying to honor Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93, which crashed into a Pennsylvania field after passengers and crew fought back against the hijackers. Her final phone call to her husband moved the crowd.

"I hope to be able to see your face again, baby. I love you, bye," Lyles said in her last call.

Jerome Sangalli, a United Airlines International Purser AFA-CWA Boston and former union vice-president, described the emotional impact of hearing her words. "I held it together until I heard that phone call. I was just rushed back to when 9/11 happened," Sangalli said. "All the flight attendants, all the pilots, they're all angels."

Dennis McWilliams, who lost four family members on 9/11, shared how his family has used their tragic memories to strengthen their bond. "Our family has taken a stance to use those awful tragic memories at our family reunions, at our weddings, at our funerals to bring ourselves closer to one another," McWilliams said.

The ceremony carried a message of unity, encouraging attendees to remember the sense of togetherness felt after the attacks. "I think we should use the memories of 9/11 to unite our country again, to remember those feelings of pride that we had in the immediate aftermath of such a tragic loss," McWilliams said.

Fort Pierce Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky echoed the call for unity. "At the end of the day, we need to come back together as we did on that fateful day and months and years after. The United States has to come back together," Dzadovsky said.

hero.headline: Maryland man arrested in Martin County on child sex charges after Roblox chat with 12-year-old bonds out
hero.teaser: A 22-year-old Maryland man arrested in Martin County on charges related to an inappropriate online relationship with a 12-year-old girl has bonded out of jail. Investigators are probing possible additional victims.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old Maryland man arrested in Martin County on charges related to an inappropriate online relationship with a 12-year-old girl has bonded out of jail after posting a $30,000 bond. Ting Bawi was booked into the Martin County Jail on Wednesday following an investigation that began with a tip alleging he was sending inappropriate messages and requesting explicit photos from a teenager.

Bawi met the victim through the online game Roblox, where she had claimed to be 16, according to the arrest report. The victim told investigators during an interview in Martin County that she and Bawi began communicating in 2025. Text messages included in the report show Bawi writing, "You belong to me," "I can't wait to have you in my possession," and expressing a desire to "make a kid" with her. Officials said their conversations made it clear she was in middle school.

Officials said they discovered child sexual abuse material on Bawi's phone. Investigators are probing the possibility of additional victims.

Investigators in Baltimore County did not charge Bawi with sexual solicitation of a minor, as Maryland's age of consent is 16, which the victim had listed on her Roblox account. Bawi faces charges in Martin County related to the inappropriate online relationship with the minor.

Martin County High School students and staff returned to class Thursday afternoon after a bomb threat email prompted an evacuation and campus-wide search. The Martin County Sheriff's Office completed a sweep of the school and found no evidence of a threat, clearing the campus to resume normal operations.

School officials notified families of the bomb threat Thursday afternoon and ordered an evacuation as law enforcement responded. Students and staff remained away from campus buildings while authorities conducted a comprehensive search of the school property.

At 2:55 p.m., school administrators sent an update confirming the Sheriff's Office had finalized its sweep and found nothing suspicious. Students and staff returned to their classrooms, and regular dismissal proceeded as scheduled. Bus transportation operated without delays.

"Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we worked with law enforcement to ensure the safety of our students and staff," school officials said in the message to families. Authorities have not released additional details about the source of the email threat. The investigation continues.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport completes $3 million renovation with dual baggage claim gates
hero.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed a $3 million renovation project designed to improve the travel experience for passengers. The upgrades include two baggage claim gates, covered walkways, a new courtyard, and canopies over passenger areas.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said the new baggage claim system allows passengers to pick up their bags within 100 feet of where the aircraft arrives. The renovations also include a new courtyard with seating where passengers can wait for their flights, along with canopies over the passenger walkways and baggage claim areas.

Passenger Austin Garafola described the changes. "Oh, it's definitely a lot better than it was. You go right in right under the awning, and then everything is so much better. We used to have to wait in single file coming out; you get rained on, you get everything, but yeah, significantly better," Garafola said. Passenger Doris Newell added, "The facility is great. The accessibility to getting here is great; it's wonderful."

Airport officials announced plans for a concession area for departing passengers, and new long-term parking has been approved. The airport serves three commercial airlines: American, JetBlue and Breeze. Officials said there has been discussion about a new terminal, with public input expected to be sought later this year. "A better experience for the passengers as they are waiting for their flight. It's going to just create a better experience for them," Dambeck said.

hero.headline: Bomb threat forces evacuation at Indian River State College in Fort Pierce
hero.teaser: Police evacuated three buildings at IRSC's Massey Campus on Friday morning after a staff member opened a threatening email. No explosives were found, and the FBI is now tracing the email's origin.
hero.body:
Police evacuated three buildings at Indian River State College's Massey Campus in Fort Pierce on Friday morning after a bomb threat was emailed to the campus, though no explosives were found. A staff member opened the email shortly before 9 a.m. and immediately notified campus security, according to Fort Pierce police.

Officers evacuated three buildings identified in the message, including the library, and conducted thorough searches. St. Lucie police and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office assisted in the search. Barbara Rubin-Perry, who was inside the college at the time, said she was really scared more than anybody else there.

Police said the email appears similar in format to threats reported in Martin County on Thursday, though they cannot directly connect the incidents. The FBI is now working with local investigators to trace the email's origin.

Michael Santiago of the Fort Pierce Police Department said such threats disrupt classes and divert officers from other duties. "We're disrupting a school, all of the students, all of the faculty. So once we narrow this down, for those who are making these threats, we will find you and we will prosecute you," Santiago said. He added that police dedicate significant resources to these threats because they never know if one might be real. The campus is expected to resume normal operations on Monday.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after bomb squad removes 8 explosive devices from home
cards.body:
A 57-year-old Fort Pierce man is in custody after investigators found eight improvised explosive devices at his home while serving a risk protection order Thursday.

Keith Anthony Morrone was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives — possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices. A judge granted the risk protection order after finding reasonable cause to believe Morrone posed a significant danger to himself or others. The court document states Morrone had recently been involved in an act or threat of violence and had recently used or threatened to use a weapon. The order required Morrone to surrender his firearms and ammunition immediately.

The investigation began Thursday around 12:20 p.m. when detectives identified suspected destructive devices at a residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. Morrone allowed deputies to search his home and car to retrieve weapons and ammunition in accordance with the order. During that search, detectives saw what appeared to be military-style hand grenades inside the house, prompting the sheriff's bomb squad to respond. Deputies say seven devices appearing to be replica hand grenades were modified, and investigators say Morrone admitted to tampering with them.

Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team. After bomb technicians arrived, the sheriff's office said they safely removed seven devices from the residence. After obtaining a search warrant for the home, investigators found an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. Investigators also located a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken from the home related to the risk protection order.

Neighbors said the street was closed for roughly 10 to 14 hours Thursday as investigators removed the explosives from the home. Morrone is currently being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond. hero.headline: Bomb threat email prompts evacuation at Martin County High School, traced to hacked Stuart account
hero.body:
A bomb threat email sent Thursday afternoon triggered the evacuation of Martin County High School and a law enforcement response involving the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the school district, and the FBI's tip line. Investigators traced the email to a hacked account at a home in Stuart, with evidence suggesting the attack originated from Russia and may be linked to a pattern of swatting cases.

Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the threatening email claimed three bombs had been planted at the school and would detonate by 2:30 p.m. or 3 p.m. The message included the name of a specific male and a location for the devices.

Investigators traced the email address to a Stuart residence. Budensiek said the account holder appears to be a victim whose email was compromised. The individual is from Ukraine, and the email originated from Russia. Deputies went to the home, and the resident has cooperated with the investigation. Budensiek said forensic analysis is underway to confirm the hacking and verify the Russian origin of the message.

The sheriff said the incident fits a trend of swatting cases the agency has encountered. The school was evacuated, parents were notified, and deputies swept the campus. After determining there was no credible threat, the school day resumed. Budensiek emphasized that public safety is his top priority.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk shares 9/11 story after 25 years
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk, a former NYPD officer who worked at the World Trade Center site after the 9/11 attacks, is speaking publicly about his experience for the first time in decades.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk, a former New York police officer who worked the World Trade Center wreckage after the September 11 attacks and lost a childhood friend in the disaster, is breaking decades of silence to share his story as the city marks 25 years since the attacks.

Niemczyk was a Queens police officer assigned to the South Auto larceny unit when terrorists attacked the World Trade Center on Sept. 11, 2001. He was completing a night shift when he responded to the Trade Center. In the direct aftermath of the attacks, Niemczyk worked sometimes seven days a week in 12-hour shifts sifting through wreckage for survivors.

"I spent probably 20 or so years hiding from Sept. 11. I made sure I wasn't working. I didn't turn on a television. I didn't look at a newspaper. I just pretended to stick my head in the sand. I coped that way for a long time," Niemczyk told WPTV anchor Mike Trim during an interview at Port St. Lucie Police headquarters.

Among those Niemczyk was searching for was a childhood friend named Mark, a New York City transit district police officer. Mark's family asked Niemczyk to relay any news from the attack site. "I knew right away. Because what I knew about the site and what I was looking at when I was there, and if anybody wasn't already reaching out and saying, 'Hey, I'm OK,' you knew," Niemczyk said.

Niemczyk said he now feels it is important to speak openly about his work at the site to honor all lives lost, including those who later developed health conditions from working in the aftermath. "You're a cop and you don't think about your own well-being first. You think about the people you're trying to save and protect, right?" he said.

Port St. Lucie has two World Trade Center beams on display, one at Tradition Field and another outside the MidFlorida Event Center.

hero.headline: Martin County marks 9/11 anniversary with Palm City bridge walk calling for unity
hero.teaser: County leaders and residents crossed Veterans Memorial Bridge in Palm City on Friday carrying photographs of attack victims as speakers urged a return to the cooperation felt immediately after Sept. 11, 2001.
hero.body:
Martin County marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks Friday with the annual Memorial Bridge Walk at Jock Leighton Park near Veterans Memorial Bridge in Palm City, where county leaders and first responders called for a return to the unity felt in the days after the attacks.

The event honored the nearly 3,000 people killed during the attacks on the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and aboard hijacked airplanes. Participants crossed Veterans Memorial Bridge carrying photographs representing nearly every person who died.

Martin County Commission Chair Sarah Heard said the country responded with "unity, civility, respect, cooperation, generosity" following the attacks. "We united. We were the United States. This is what I choose to remember," Heard said.

Commissioner Stacey Hetherington reflected on the sense of togetherness Americans experienced after the attacks. "September 12th is also remembered because we united, we came together and we worked in unity," Hetherington said.

Community volunteer Mayce DelValle, who helped organize the memorial walk, carried photographs honoring Mark Zepplin and Kevin Marlowe, people she personally knew who died in the Twin Towers. "These guys were like family to me," DelValle said. "They unfortunately lost their lives in the buildings at the Twin Towers at Ground Zero on that day."

DelValle said one of the most powerful parts of the event was seeing younger generations participate. "It is so important that the young people really understand and never forget those people who lost their lives," DelValle said. "I feel like it's our responsibility as people that were around on 9/11 to make sure people understand what really happened."

Martin County Fire Rescue Chief Chad Cianciulli described the patriotism that emerged immediately following the attacks. "That was a day to be proud to be American," Cianciulli said while discussing Sept. 12, 2001.

Chaplain Hoss Wiggins led a prayer before the walk. "After that awful event, the next day, a nation united in prayer," Wiggins said. "They set aside their differences and they united, and they cried out to God Almighty for help."

Wiggins said memorial events taking place across the country serve as reminders not to forget the sacrifices made by victims, first responders and military members. "The word of God encourages us over and over and over again to remember or don't forget," Wiggins said. "And that's what we're here today to do is to remember those who paid the ultimate sacrifice."

cards.headline: Martin County High School evacuated Thursday after emailed bomb threat
cards.teaser: Martin County High School evacuated all students and staff Thursday afternoon after receiving a bomb threat by email. The Martin County Sheriff's Office found no evidence of danger after a comprehensive search.
cards.body:
Martin County High School evacuated all students and staff Thursday afternoon after receiving a bomb threat by email. The Martin County Sheriff's Office completed a comprehensive search of the campus and found no evidence of a threat.

The school notified parents of the increased law enforcement presence on campus in response to the bomb threat sent by email Thursday afternoon. All students and staff were evacuated from campus buildings while deputies conducted the search.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office completed its final sweep just before 3 p.m. and found no evidence of a threat. Students and staff returned to their classrooms after the all-clear.

The high school announced on Facebook that regular dismissal procedures continued as scheduled. Bus transportation operated without delay.
cards.article_text: By: Aja Dorsainvil Posted and last updated MARTIN COUNTY, Fla. — The Martin County Sheriff's Office said it found no evidence of a threat after sweeping Martin County High School following a bomb threat. The school said it was evacuated Thursday afternoon. "Please be advised that there is an increased law enforcement presence on campus in response to a bomb threat that was sent in via email this afternoon," the school said. All students and staff were evacuated from campus buildings, while the Martin County Sheriff's Office conducted a comprehensive search of the property. The high school said the sheriff's office conducted its final sweep just before 3 p.m. and found no evidence of a threat. "Students and staff are returning to their classrooms, and regular dismissal procedures will continue as scheduled. Bus transportation is expected to operate without delay," the high school said in a Facebook post .

cards.headline: Martin County High School bomb threat now believed to have originated from Russia
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed Friday that investigators suspect a bomb threat that prompted the evacuation of Martin County High School Thursday afternoon originated from Russia.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after deputies find 8 suspected explosive devices at home
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man Thursday after deputies serving a risk protection order found eight suspected explosive devices and bomb-making materials at his home near Balsam Drive.

Deputies with the Targeted Violence Unit went to the residence at about 12:20 p.m. Thursday to serve the risk protection order when they identified numerous suspected destructive devices. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the Bomb Disposal Team. Bomb technicians removed seven suspected destructive devices from the home and placed them in a containment vessel. After obtaining a search warrant, deputies found and safely removed an eighth suspected explosive device, along with a large quantity of materials used to make explosive devices. Eight firearms were also seized from the home as part of the risk protection order.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the investigation underscores the seriousness of what detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to threats. Del Toro praised the Targeted Violence Unit detectives for recognizing the potential danger and taking immediate action, and the Bomb Disposal Team technicians for putting themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove the devices. Del Toro said he is grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as the investigation continues.

Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, was charged with eight counts of possessing, making or attempting to make a destructive device. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond. The investigation remains ongoing. The sheriff's office said there is no immediate threat to the community.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie holds 25th anniversary 9/11 remembrance ceremony Friday morning
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie will honor victims, survivors and first responders of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks at a remembrance ceremony Friday morning at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie will hold its annual 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony at 8:30 a.m. Friday at the Memorial Fountain at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center, located at 9221 Event Center Place. The ceremony marks 25 years since the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

City officials said the ceremony will serve as a time for reflection while honoring the lives lost on Sept. 11, 2001, and recognizing the strength and unity shown in the years since.

Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin, Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk and St. Lucie County Fire District Firefighter/Paramedic Allen Civita will deliver remarks. Port St. Lucie Police Department Chaplain Nick Manzie will deliver an invocation. Retired New York City Police Department detective Rafael Diaz will serve as the guest speaker.

The Port St. Lucie High School Choir will perform during the ceremony. The St. Lucie County Fire District, Port St. Lucie Police Department and St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office are expected to participate. Following the ceremony, attendees are invited inside the MIDFLORIDA Event Center for light refreshments.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County advances P1 Motor Club water agreement, orders policy review
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County commissioners agreed Tuesday to move forward with a bulk water service agreement for the 650-acre P1 Motor Club racetrack development while directing staff to conduct a year-long review of utility capacity policies.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County commissioners agreed Tuesday to move forward with a bulk water service agreement for the 650-acre P1 Motor Club racetrack development while directing staff to conduct a year-long review of utility capacity policies. The decision came during the Board of County Commissioners' Sept. 8 informal meeting, where officials debated how the St. Lucie County Water and Sewer District should calculate water capacity for the motorsports project.

County staff calculated Phase 1 of the project at 126 equivalent residential connections, or ERCs, under the district's current methodology. P1 representatives argued the project's water demand should be lower than a traditional residential development because its garage-townhome units are intended for occasional or seasonal use. Staff countered that the units are built to residential standards, with kitchens and living areas, and that the district must reserve enough capacity to protect the utility system.

Commissioners agreed to pursue a bulk water agreement using the current ERC methodology to determine the project's daily water allocation. The agreement would allow P1 to manage water distribution within the project while the county retains safeguards for the utility system. The board also directed staff to begin a formal review of the county's Uniform Extension Policy and other utility-service standards, including whether bulk agreements or alternative calculation methods should be addressed for specialized developments. Staff was asked to complete that policy work within a year.

P1 Motor Club is planned on a 650-acre former citrus grove west of Port St. Lucie. The private, members-only development is planned to include two racetracks, 125 condos and custom garages. The P1 website describes plans for more than nine miles of private track space, including a 4.5-mile P1 Circuit and a 3-mile Treasure Coast Circuit, as well as karting, rally and drift courses. The proposed development also includes trackside residences, garage townhomes, a clubhouse, event space and a motorsports-related commerce park. The site advertises its garage townhomes with full kitchens, living and dining areas, along with unlimited overnight stays for owners, families and guests.

hero.headline: Bomb squad, FBI respond to Fort Pierce home after suspected devices found
hero.body:
The bomb squad, FBI agents, and federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms agents surrounded a Fort Pierce home Thursday after St. Lucie County sheriff's deputies discovered suspected destructive devices while serving a risk protection order. One person was detained pending investigation.

Deputies went to a home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive around 12:20 p.m. Thursday to serve a risk protection order, a legal order temporarily restricting someone from possessing firearms. Deputies backed out of the home, called the bomb squad, and notified federal authorities. The bomb squad secured the items in the back of the bomb disposal vehicle. Investigators did not disclose what the destructive devices were.

cards.headline: Former Fort Pierce police officer arrested on felony charges for tracking ex-girlfriend with police databases
cards.teaser: Josepher Crutchfield faces four felony charges after allegedly conducting more than 400 searches to monitor an ex-girlfriend's vehicle from October 2022 to July 2023. Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith announced new restrictions on database access following the arrest.
cards.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond after being charged with four felonies for allegedly misusing police databases to track an ex-girlfriend.

Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith said Tuesday that from October 2022 to July 2023, Crutchfield used four different police databases to monitor a single vehicle. Crutchfield conducted more than 400 searches, using Flock cameras 382 times, which allowed him to track the victim's location and movements, according to the police report. The registered owner of that vehicle was an ex-girlfriend, Smith said.

Most of the queries were made when Crutchfield was off duty, Smith said. Crutchfield resigned from the department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation.

Smith called the arrest a black eye for the department but emphasized investigators did what had to be done. He announced changes to department policies regarding police database access, limiting who can access them and requiring permission from a deputy chief for all searches.

This is a difficult moment for our organization and our community, Smith said Tuesday. Conduct alleged in this case is unacceptable and represents a serious breach in the trust that's placed in law enforcement, Smith said. When there is credible evidence that an officer may have violated the law, we have an obligation to act. The badge does not provide immunity from accountability, Smith said.

hero.headline: Stuart commission votes 3-2 to rehire Michael Mortell as city manager
hero.body:
The Stuart City Commission voted 3-2 Wednesday evening to rehire former City Manager Michael Mortell at a roughly $225,000 salary, pending his agreement to a new contract that restricts outside work and requires monthly reporting to commissioners. The decision came just two weeks after the commission dismissed City Manager Michael Giardino, drawing significant pushback from residents who criticized the transparency of the leadership change.

The new contract includes a salary lower than the more than $265,000 Mortell previously earned as city manager. The contract also includes conditions restricting the use of city resources for outside work and requiring the city's HR director to report any outside work to commissioners on a monthly basis.

Resident Deana Peterson told commissioners the transparency was not given to the citizens of Stuart. "This amounts to nothing more than petty cronyism and hypocrisy. All of you who supported Mr. Giardino's firing should be ashamed of yourselves," Peterson said. Resident Robin Cartwright pushed back on the commission's characterization of Giardino's tenure, saying Giardino was struggling with the stalemate that the commission presented. "For any commissioner up here to say that someone failed at their job I would say that you failed at your job," Cartwright said. Resident David Kelman urged the commission to reconsider its approach. "You all represent this city. You need to step back and unite because what you're doing ain't going to work. It's three versus two here," Kelman said.

Commissioner Campbell Rich called for contract negotiations with Mortell at the previous meeting, citing his institutional knowledge. "This is not the time for someone with training wheels to negotiate us through that very difficult period. We need the most experience we can possibly get," Rich said. Commissioners Sean Reed and Laura Giobbi raised ethical concerns about the rehiring. Reed questioned the process, saying it was a disservice to constituents that the commission was taking action on a potential city manager but the individual was not present to be questioned. Giobbi pointed to the broader divisions within the community. "The community is broken. The community is so divided it's sad," Giobbi said. Reed closed the meeting with a motion to add an Oct. 12 agenda item to discuss foregoing commissioner salaries for two years to offset costs related to city manager turnover.

cards.headline: Martin County High School evacuated after emailed bomb threat
cards.teaser: Martin County High School was evacuated Thursday afternoon after a bomb threat was sent via email. The Martin County Sheriff's Office swept the campus and found no evidence of a threat.
cards.body:
Martin County High School was evacuated Thursday afternoon after a bomb threat was sent via email. The Martin County Sheriff's Office swept the campus and found no evidence of a threat.

All students and staff were evacuated from campus buildings while the sheriff's office conducted a comprehensive search of the property. The sheriff's office completed its final sweep just before 3 p.m.

Students and staff returned to their classrooms after the sweep. Regular dismissal procedures continued as scheduled, and bus transportation operated without delay, the high school said in a Facebook post.

All students and staff were evacuated from campus buildings, while the Martin County Sheriff's Office conducted a comprehensive search of the property. The high school said the sheriff's office conducted its final sweep just before 3 p.m. and found no evidence of a threat. "Students and staff are returning to their classrooms, and regular dismissal procedures will continue as scheduled. Bus transportation is expected to operate without delay," the high school said in a Facebook post .

hero.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport completes $3M upgrades, plans fall terminal expansion input
hero.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed nearly $3 million in improvements and will launch a community input process this fall on potential terminal expansion designs, interim airport director Brandon Dambeck said. The completed upgrades include new shaded walkways, a turf patio, and a redesigned baggage claim area.

The improvements are designed to improve the experience for travelers coming in and out of Vero Beach, Dambeck said. New shaded walkways were added for arrivals and departures, along with a shaded baggage claim area with seating. The shade structures are built for Florida's intense sun and are 90 percent-plus UV rated, Dambeck said.

Among the new additions is a turf patio with outdoor furniture. A concession stand is also coming, giving travelers a place to grab a bite and a drink. Passengers will be able to relax and sip a drink while waiting, Dambeck said.

This fall, the airport plans to invite the community to weigh in on potential designs for a terminal expansion. One design would bring the baggage claim indoors. The airport wants to make sure community members have their voice included in the decisions that are ultimately being made to an asset of the city, Dambeck said.

The improvements come after JetBlue announced it was discontinuing its direct flight from Vero Beach to New York's JFK airport. The need is still here for these improvements, Dambeck said.

New flights could be on the horizon, including flights with Breeze to Pittsburgh and American Airlines to Philadelphia, Dambeck said. Jill, a traveler who was returning from Boston, said she is optimistic about the airport's future. She thinks it's going to get a lot more business and they're just going to keep expanding, she said.

hero.headline: Bomb squad, FBI respond after deputies find suspected destructive devices at Fort Pierce home
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office bomb squad and federal agents surrounded a Fort Pierce home Thursday after deputies serving a risk protection order discovered suspected destructive devices inside. Deputies went to a home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive around 12:20 p.m. to serve the order, which temporarily restricts someone from possessing firearms.

Deputies found items beyond what they expected during the service of the order. "They came across a box of items that were indicative of being destructive devices," said Capt. Bolonka of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Deputies backed out of the home and called the bomb squad. Agents from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms also responded to the scene.

The bomb squad secured the items in the back of the bomb disposal vehicle. "At this point in time, they have one individual detained pending this investigation," Bolonka said. Investigators have not disclosed what the destructive devices were.

Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for ten years, expressed concern about the situation. "That's really bad," Rates said. He described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," he said.

cards.headline: Former Fort Pierce officer jailed on $80,000 bond for tracking ex-girlfriend
cards.teaser: A former Fort Pierce police officer is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond after being charged with four felonies for allegedly misusing police databases to track an ex-girlfriend.
cards.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond after being charged with four felonies for allegedly misusing police databases to track an ex-girlfriend.

Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith said Tuesday that from October 2022 to July 2023, Crutchfield used four different police databases to monitor a single vehicle. The registered owner of that vehicle was an ex-girlfriend. Most of the queries were made when Crutchfield was off duty.

According to the police report, Crutchfield conducted more than 400 searches, using Flock cameras 382 times. The searches allowed him to track the victim's location and movements.

Crutchfield resigned from the department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation. Smith called the arrest a black eye for the department but said investigators had an obligation to act when there is credible evidence an officer may have violated the law. Smith announced changes to department policies regarding police database access, limiting who can access them and requiring permission from a deputy chief for all searches.

hero.headline: Former Fort Pierce officer jailed on $80,000 bond after stalking ex-girlfriend with police databases
hero.teaser: Josepher Crutchfield faces four felony charges after allegedly using police databases more than 400 times to track an ex-girlfriend's vehicle, including 382 searches through Flock cameras.
hero.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond after being charged with four felonies for allegedly misusing police databases to track an ex-girlfriend. Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith said Tuesday that from October 2022 to July 2023, Crutchfield used four different police databases to monitor a single vehicle. The registered owner of that vehicle was an ex-girlfriend, according to Smith.

According to the police report, Crutchfield conducted more than 400 searches, using Flock cameras 382 times, which allowed him to track the victim's location and movements. Smith said most of these queries were made when Crutchfield was off duty.

Crutchfield resigned from the department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation, Smith said. The chief called the arrest a black eye for the department but emphasized investigators did what had to be done.

"Conduct alleged in this case is unacceptable and represents a serious breach in the trust that's placed in law enforcement," Smith said. "When there is credible evidence that an officer may have violated the law, we have an obligation to act. The badge does not provide immunity from accountability."

Smith announced changes to department policies regarding police database access, limiting who can access them and requiring permission from a deputy chief for all searches. "This is a difficult moment for our organization and our community," Smith said.

The sheriff's office completed its final sweep just before 3 p.m. Students and staff returned to their classrooms, and regular dismissal procedures continued as scheduled. Bus transportation operated without delay, the high school said in a Facebook post.
