cards.headline: Two arrested in Indian River County over Labor Day weekend for illegal saw palmetto harvesting
cards.teaser: Indian River County deputies arrested two men in separate cases involving alleged illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over the Labor Day weekend, one involving a forged permit and the other for harvesting an endangered plant without a permit.
cards.body:
Indian River County deputies arrested two men in separate cases involving alleged illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over the Labor Day weekend, according to arrest affidavits. The arrests add to a series of recent saw palmetto berry cases across the Treasure Coast involving hundreds of pounds of berries.

Corey Michael Smith of Vero Beach was arrested Sept. 4 after deputies responded to a trespassing call at a BP gas station on 9th Street Southwest, the affidavit states. A deputy said a helicopter crew had spotted Smith on Indian River County School Board property near 800 20th Ave. Deputies found him at the gas station with five black bags containing saw palmetto stalks, according to the affidavit.

Smith allegedly showed deputies a palmetto berry harvesting permit that listed an address on 17th Avenue Southwest. The property owner told deputies Smith did not have permission to harvest on the property, which belongs to the Salvation Army, the affidavit says. Smith was arrested on charges of using a false or forged palmetto berry harvest permit, disclosing police radio information to aid a suspect, and trespassing after a warning. The affidavit states a deputy heard dispatch traffic coming from a scanner app on Smith's phone while he was detained.

A day later, deputies arrested Francis Ostrowski after a sheriff's office camera in the North County Conservation Area near 7800 130th St. captured a man carrying a bag filled with saw palmetto berries, according to his affidavit. Deputies located Ostrowski nearby with a bag of berries and asked whether he had a permit to harvest them. Ostrowski said he did not, the affidavit states. Ostrowski was arrested on a felony charge of harvesting an endangered plant without a permit.

CBS12 previously reported on arrests involving the alleged theft of about 200 pounds of berries in Martin County and about 150 pounds in Indian River County. In another recent case, a Boynton Beach man was arrested after deputies said they found about 500 pounds of saw palmetto berries.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport completes nearly $3 million in upgrades
hero.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed nearly $3 million in improvements, adding new shaded walkways, a turf patio and a redesigned baggage claim area. The airport also plans to invite the community this fall to weigh in on potential designs for a terminal expansion.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the upgrades are designed to improve the experience for travelers coming in and out of Vero Beach. Among the new additions is a turf patio with outdoor furniture, and a concession stand is also coming to give travelers a place to grab a bite and a drink. New shaded walkways were added for arrivals and departures, along with a shaded baggage claim area with seating. Dambeck said the shade structures are built for Florida's intense sun and are 90 percent-plus UV rated. Travelers can sit on benches while they wait for their bags to be brought around to the gate.

One terminal expansion design under consideration would bring the baggage claim indoors. Dambeck said the airport wants to make sure the community has its voice included in the decisions that are ultimately being made to an asset of the city. The fall community input sessions will allow residents to weigh in on the potential designs before any final decisions are made about the expansion.

The improvements come after JetBlue announced it was discontinuing its direct flight from Vero Beach to New York's JFK airport. Dambeck said the need is still here for these improvements. He said new flights could be on the horizon, including flights with Breeze to Pittsburgh and American Airlines to Philadelphia. Jill, a traveler who was returning from Boston, said she is optimistic about the airport's future. She thinks it is going to get a lot more business and the airport will just keep expanding.

cards.headline: Vero Beach gym owner Paige Vasser wins gold with Team USA in France paintball event
cards.teaser: Paige Vasser, owner of Legacy Boxing Gym in Vero Beach, helped Team USA win gold at an international paintball event in France last weekend. She is now ranked among the top 10 professional women in paintball despite never playing a sport until age 21.
cards.body:
Paige Vasser, owner of Legacy Boxing Gym in Vero Beach, helped Team USA win gold at an international paintball event in France last weekend. She is now ranked among the top 10 professional women in paintball despite never playing a sport until she was 21 years old.

Vasser grew up in Southeast Georgia near Brunswick before moving to Sebastian, where she eventually opened Legacy Boxing Gym in Vero Beach to give back to the community. Her introduction to sports came through boxing at age 21. She had never exercised or played sports before taking up boxing, which she said she thought was "badass." Her boyfriend, who had been playing paintball for about 10 years, later introduced her to the sport.

As the gym's owner looking for more activities, Vasser took her team at Legacy for a day of paintballing and quickly fell in love with it. The group ended up enjoying it on weekends as something that kept them busy. What started as a weekend hobby quickly turned into something much bigger when a coach noticed Vasser playing and recruited her for his divisional team. A year later, she signed with her first women's professional team. Her rise through the sport has been rapid.

Last weekend, Vasser flew into Paris and competed at an event in France held at the site of the United Paintball Federation. Team USA won gold in one of the largest events in the sport. Vasser played with teammates she had never played with before. She said the experience was awesome and that the other players were amazing and it was a lot of fun.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police investigating death of unidentified man found near Okeechobee Road business
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are investigating after an unidentified man was found dead in the grass near a business on Okeechobee Road Wednesday morning.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police are investigating after an unidentified man was found dead in the grass near a business on Okeechobee Road Wednesday morning.

Officers responded to the 7000 block of Okeechobee Road shortly before 7 a.m. after receiving reports of an unresponsive man lying in the grass near a business. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue also responded and the man was pronounced dead at the scene. A witness told investigators they had seen the man lying in the same area the night before but believed he was sleeping.

Detectives found no obvious signs of foul play. The Medical Examiner's Office will determine the cause and manner of death. Detectives are working to identify the man and the investigation remains active.

hero.headline: Maryland man arrested in Martin County on child sex charges after Roblox chat with 12-year-old
hero.body:
A Maryland man was arrested in Martin County on charges related to an inappropriate online relationship with a 12-year-old girl he met through the video game Roblox, according to investigators. Ting Bawi, 22, was booked into the Martin County Jail on Wednesday on a warrant. Officials said they discovered child sexual abuse material on his phone and are investigating the possibility of additional victims.

The investigation began with a tip alleging Bawi was sending inappropriate messages and requesting explicit photos from a teenager, according to the arrest report. The victim told investigators in Martin County that she and Bawi began communicating in 2025. She had claimed to be 16 on Roblox, but officials said their conversations made it clear she was in middle school.

Text messages included in the report show Bawi writing to the girl, "You belong to me," "I can't wait to have you in my possession," and expressing a desire to "make a kid" with her, according to investigators.

Investigators in Baltimore County did not charge Bawi with sexual solicitation of a minor because Maryland's age of consent is 16, which the victim had listed on her Roblox account. Bawi was held on a $30,000 bond in Martin County and has since bonded out.

hero.headline: Donalds attacks Jolly as socialist, Democrats counter with donor ties in Florida governor's race
hero.body:
Florida's governor's race has sharpened into competing attacks over ideology and influence as Republican Byron Donalds portrays Democrat David Jolly as an ally of socialism while Jolly counters by alleging donors are buying control of the Republican nominee.

The escalating fight arrives as voters typically begin paying closer attention after Labor Day, according to political analyst Susan MacManus. At the GOP's midterm convention in Dallas on Wednesday, Donalds accused Jolly of embracing "radical socialism" and singled out Jolly's proposal for public hurricane coverage, describing it as a government takeover of property insurance that would leave Floridians paying a new tax. Donalds argued the costs would reach beyond coastal homeowners to renters and other insurance customers. "This election cycle is about one thing: common sense versus crazy," Donalds said.

Jolly fired back by targeting Donalds' financial backers. "The same people that have owned Tallahassee for 30 years are buying Byron right now, because they want to control Tallahassee, not because they care about Byron," Jolly said in an online video. Jolly framed his campaign as a chance to disrupt that power, arguing that a coalition seeking change could overcome Donalds' financial advantage. Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried accused Donalds during a virtual news conference Wednesday of supporting President Donald Trump's policies at Floridians' expense. "Let me be clear: there is nothing about this record that is worth celebrating," Fried said.

The ideological theme continued Thursday at Miami's Bay of Pigs Museum, where Gov. Ron DeSantis promoted classroom lessons about the dangers of communism. Donalds' running mate, former state Sen. Bryan Avila, joined DeSantis and accused Democrats of promoting socialist policies, invoking his family's experience fleeing communist Cuba. "In fact, I've offered several of them to give them a one-way trip to Cuba, so that they understand the horrors of communism," Avila said. The Republican attacks also extend to state Rep. Angie Nixon, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, who joined the Democratic Socialists of America in June, according to PolitiFact's reporting published by WLRN.

MacManus said campaigns time their strongest messages to when people are preparing to cast ballots. "There's an old saying that you save your best ads and strategies for right at the point when people actually begin casting ballots," MacManus said. But getting voters' attention is only part of the challenge, she said, as distrust of politics and lower participation in midterm elections make turnout difficult. "The game is absolutely turnout," MacManus said.

hero.headline: Vero Beach gym owner wins gold with Team USA at international paintball event in France
hero.body:
Paige Vasser, owner of Legacy Boxing Gym in Vero Beach, won gold with Team USA at an international paintball event in France last weekend, capping a rapid rise that took her from first-time athlete at 21 to one of the top 10 professional women in the sport.

Vasser grew up in Southeast Georgia near Brunswick before moving to Sebastian, where she eventually opened Legacy Boxing Gym in Vero Beach to give back to the community. She never played a sport until she was 21 years old, when she took up boxing. Boxing was her first introduction to sports and exercise. Her boyfriend, who had been playing paintball for about 10 years, later introduced her to that sport. She had never even heard of paintball before meeting him. Vasser took her team at Legacy for a day of paintballing and quickly fell in love with it as a weekend activity.

What started as a weekend hobby quickly turned into something much bigger. A coach noticed Vasser playing and recruited her for his divisional team. A year later, she signed with her first women's professional team. Her rise through the sport has been rapid, and she is now ranked among the top professional women in paintball.

The event in France was held at the site of the United Paintball Federation, one of the largest events in the sport. Vasser flew into Paris for the competition, where Team USA won gold. She got to play with teammates she had never played with before. "I got to play with girls that I never get to play with before, which is an awesome experience. They're amazing, and it was a lot of fun," Vasser said. The achievement marks a remarkable journey for someone who never participated in sports until adulthood and highlights her dedication to athletic competition in both boxing and paintball.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police investigate death of unidentified man found near Okeechobee Road business
hero.teaser: Fort Pierce police are investigating after an unidentified man was found dead in the grass near a business on Okeechobee Road Wednesday morning.
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police are investigating the death of an unidentified man who was found lying in the grass near a business on Okeechobee Road Wednesday morning.

Officers responded to the 7000 block of Okeechobee Road shortly before 7 a.m. after receiving reports of an unresponsive man lying in the grass near a business. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue also responded and the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

A witness told investigators they had seen the man lying in the same area the night before but believed he was sleeping. Detectives found no obvious signs of foul play. The Medical Examiner's Office will determine the cause and manner of death. Detectives are working to identify the man and the investigation remains active.

cards.headline: Ex-Fort Pierce officer Josepher Crutchfield charged with four felonies for tracking ex-girlfriend
cards.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond after being charged with four felonies for allegedly misusing police databases to track an ex-girlfriend. Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith announced Tuesday that Crutchfield conducted more than 400 searches from October 2022 to July 2023 to monitor a single vehicle registered to an ex-girlfriend.

Crutchfield used Flock cameras 382 times to track the victim's location and movements, according to the police report. He accessed four different police databases during the nine-month period, with most queries made while he was off duty.

"Conduct alleged in this case is unacceptable and represents a serious breach in the trust that's placed in law enforcement," Smith said. "When there is credible evidence that an officer may have violated the law, we have an obligation to act. The badge does not provide immunity from accountability."

Crutchfield resigned from the Fort Pierce Police Department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation. Smith called the arrest a black eye for the department but emphasized investigators fulfilled their obligation. "This is a difficult moment for our organization and our community," Smith said.

Smith announced changes to department policies regarding police database access in the wake of the case. The new policies limit who can access the databases and require permission from a deputy chief for all searches.

hero.headline: Martin County High School evacuated after bomb threat; sweep finds no evidence
hero.body:
Martin County High School was evacuated Thursday afternoon after a bomb threat was received via email, and a sweep by the Martin County Sheriff's Office found no evidence of a threat. Students and staff returned to their classrooms and regular dismissal continued as scheduled.

School administrators notified families of an increased law enforcement presence on campus as authorities responded to the threat. The Martin County Sheriff's Office conducted a comprehensive search of the school property while students and staff remained evacuated away from campus buildings.

In an update issued at 2:55 p.m., school officials said the Martin County Sheriff's Office was finalizing its sweep of the campus and found no evidence of a threat. Students and staff were cleared to return to their classrooms, and regular dismissal procedures were expected to continue as scheduled. School officials also said bus transportation was anticipated to operate without delays.

"Please know that students and staff remain safe," the school said in its notification to families. "Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we worked with law enforcement to ensure the safety of our students and staff." Parents were notified of the situation through a message from the school Thursday afternoon. Authorities have not released additional details about the source of the email threat.

hero.headline: Florida judge recommends discipline for Boca Raton nurse over TikTok post
hero.body:
A Florida administrative law judge has recommended disciplinary action against a registered nurse who posted a TikTok video wishing a severe birth injury on White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt while she was pregnant. Judge Robert S. Cohen issued the recommended order Sept. 1, proposing a reprimand, $250 fine, and social media training for Alexis Backer Lawler, a labor and delivery nurse at Baptist Health Boca Raton Regional Hospital. The case now goes to the Board of Nursing for a final ruling.

The Florida Department of Health filed an administrative complaint against Lawler on Feb. 20 after she posted the video on Jan. 22. In the video, Lawler identified herself as a labor and delivery nurse and directed graphic, profane language at Leavitt, wishing her a fourth-degree tear. The injury was described at hearing as the most severe that can occur during childbirth, requiring surgery under anesthesia and potentially additional procedures. "As a labor and delivery nurse, it gives me great joy to wish Karoline Leavitt a fourth-degree tear," Lawler said in the video.

A final hearing was held July 14 in Tallahassee. The case centered on whether Lawler's TikTok post constituted unprofessional conduct under Florida Administrative Code Rule 64B9-8.005(14), which prohibits nurses from using abusive, threatening or foul language in front of a patient or directing such language toward a patient. Lawler argued the video was protected political speech made on her personal time, away from her workplace, and not directed at any patient.

Cohen rejected that argument after two Baptist Health labor and delivery patients testified that they had seen the video before or around the time of their own deliveries at the hospital. Patient E.G. testified that she had been assigned Lawler as her nurse during her Jan. 5–6 delivery and later saw the video shared by her husband. She described her reaction as shock and disgust. "It was just inappropriate, specifically coming from someone whose job is to take care of you at one of your most vulnerable moments," E.G. testified. Another patient testified that she saw the video a few days before her own admission to Baptist Health on Jan. 24 and overheard nurses at the hospital discussing it during her stay. She said she did not have Lawler as her nurse and that her decision to deliver at Baptist Health was not changed by having seen the video. Neither patient filed or planned to file a lawsuit against the hospital or Lawler.

Cohen found that Lawler had not taken steps to restrict her TikTok audience before posting the video and did not appear to have a clear understanding of which of her accounts were public or private. "By posting the video on TikTok, with some clearly provocative language aimed at a pregnant mom who happens to be a public figure, on a popular public social media platform, she should have known there was a risk of the posting going viral," Cohen wrote. He also noted that Lawler had identified herself as a labor and delivery nurse in the video, which he said lent specific weight to the nature of the injury she was wishing on Leavitt.

Shortly after the video circulated, Lawler was fired from Baptist Health Boca Raton Regional Hospital. A hospital spokesperson confirmed her termination, stating that the comments made in the social media video do not reflect the hospital's values or the standards expected of healthcare professionals. Lawler's TikTok account was public at the time of the posting, and a group called Libs of TikTok reposted the video along with Lawler's place of employment, causing it to spread widely. Lawler testified that she subsequently received death threats and tightened her social media privacy settings. Her TikTok account has since been banned.

The recommended order also references a separate incident from September 2025, in which Baptist Health received complaints from employees and members of the public about social media posts Lawler made related to the death of conservative commentator Charlie Kirk. Human resources records show Lawler met with hospital management, reviewed the hospital's social media policy and acknowledged the guidance. No formal discipline was issued at that time. Lawler was also noted to have worn a pin reading "no uterus, no opinion" while working in the labor and delivery unit. One patient testified that she found the pin off-putting in that setting.

In weighing the penalty, Cohen cited several mitigating factors: Lawler has been licensed for approximately 14 years with no prior disciplinary history, the two patients who testified suffered no physical harm and pursued no legal action, and Lawler lost her job at Baptist Health as a result of the incident. "The mitigating factors in this case outweigh any potential aggravating factors which were not proven to exist," Cohen wrote. Cohen also recommended the board assess costs related to the investigation and prosecution of the case. The Board of Nursing is not required to follow the judge's recommendation.

hero.headline: Vero Beach gym owner helps Team USA win gold in paintball at France event
hero.body:
Paige Vasser, owner of Legacy Boxing Gym in Vero Beach, helped Team USA win gold last weekend at an international paintball competition in France, capping a rapid rise that has placed her among the top-10 professional women in the sport.

Vasser grew up in Southeast Georgia near Brunswick before moving to Sebastian, where she eventually opened Legacy Boxing Gym in Vero Beach. She never played a sport until she was 21 years old. Her introduction to athletics came through boxing, which she embraced fully despite having never exercised before. Vasser said she thought boxing was, in her words, badass. Her boyfriend, who had been playing paintball for about 10 years, later introduced her to the sport. She took her team at Legacy for a day of paintballing and quickly fell in love with it as a weekend activity that kept them busy.

What started as a weekend hobby quickly turned into something much bigger. A coach noticed Vasser playing and recruited her for his divisional team. A year later, she signed with her first women's professional team. Her rise through the sport has been rapid, placing her among the top professional women in paintball. Last weekend she competed internationally when she flew into Paris for an event in France.

The event was held at the site of the United Paintball Federation, where Vasser and Team USA won gold in one of the largest competitions in the sport. Vasser said she got to play with girls she never played with before, calling it an awesome experience. She said the other players were amazing and it was a lot of fun. The gym owner's journey from someone who never played sports or exercised before age 21 to becoming an international gold medalist in paintball highlights her rapid development in the sport. Her story demonstrates how a weekend pastime can evolve into professional athletic success when combined with dedication and natural talent.

hero.headline: Bomb threat email prompts evacuation at Martin County High School
hero.body:
Martin County High School was evacuated Thursday afternoon following a bomb threat sent via email, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The school announced an increased law enforcement presence on campus as authorities responded to the threat.

All students and staff were evacuated from campus buildings while the Martin County Sheriff's Office conducted a comprehensive search of the property. Deputies systematically examined the school grounds to determine whether any credible danger existed. The sheriff's office completed its final sweep just before 3 p.m. and found no evidence of a threat on the premises.

Following the all-clear from law enforcement, students and staff returned to their classrooms. The high school announced in a Facebook post that regular dismissal procedures would continue as scheduled. Bus transportation was expected to operate without delay despite the earlier disruption to the school day.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed it found no evidence to substantiate the emailed bomb threat after completing its thorough search of Martin County High School. The incident required a full evacuation of the campus while deputies conducted their investigation, but normal school operations resumed once authorities determined the campus was safe. The school kept families informed throughout the situation, updating them on the law enforcement response and the eventual return to regular activities.

cards.headline: Former Fort Pierce officer charged with felonies for tracking ex-girlfriend with Flock cameras
cards.teaser: Josepher Crutchfield faces four felony charges for allegedly running more than 400 unauthorized database searches to monitor an ex-girlfriend's vehicle. He is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond.
cards.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond after being charged with four felonies for allegedly misusing police databases to track an ex-girlfriend.

Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith said Tuesday that from October 2022 to July 2023, Crutchfield used four different police databases to monitor a single vehicle. According to the police report, Crutchfield conducted more than 400 searches, using Flock cameras 382 times, which allowed him to track the victim's location and movements. Smith said most of the queries were made when Crutchfield was off duty, and investigators found that the registered owner of the vehicle was an ex-girlfriend.

"Conduct alleged in this case is unacceptable and represents a serious breach in the trust that's placed in law enforcement," Smith said.

Crutchfield resigned from the department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation. Smith called the arrest a black eye for the department but emphasized investigators did what had to be done. "When there is credible evidence that an officer may have violated the law, we have an obligation to act. The badge does not provide immunity from accountability," Smith said.

Smith also announced changes to department policies regarding police database access, limiting who can access them and requiring permission from a deputy chief for all searches. "This is a difficult moment for our organization and our community," Smith said.

cards.headline: Two arrested in Indian River County for illegal saw palmetto harvesting over Labor Day weekend
cards.teaser: Indian River County deputies arrested two men in separate cases involving alleged illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over the Labor Day weekend, one involving a forged permit and the other for harvesting an endangered plant without a permit.
cards.body:
Indian River County deputies arrested two men in separate cases involving alleged illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over the Labor Day weekend, according to arrest affidavits. The arrests are part of a broader Treasure Coast crackdown on saw palmetto berry theft.

Corey Michael Smith, of Vero Beach, was arrested Sept. 4 after deputies responded to a trespassing call at a BP gas station on 9th Street Southwest. A helicopter crew had spotted Smith on Indian River County School Board property near 800 20th Avenue. Deputies found him at the gas station with five black bags containing saw palmetto stalks, according to the affidavit. Smith showed deputies a palmetto berry harvesting permit that listed an address on 17th Avenue Southwest. The property owner told deputies Smith did not have permission to harvest on the property, which belongs to the Salvation Army. Smith was arrested on charges of using a false or forged palmetto berry harvest permit, disclosing police radio information to aid a suspect, and trespassing after a warning. A deputy heard dispatch traffic coming from a scanner app on Smith's phone while he was detained.

A day later, deputies arrested Francis Ostrowski after a sheriff's office camera in the North County Conservation Area near 7800 130th Street captured a man carrying a bag filled with saw palmetto berries, according to his affidavit. Deputies located Ostrowski nearby with a bag of berries and asked whether he had a permit to harvest them. Ostrowski said he did not. Ostrowski was arrested on a felony charge of harvesting an endangered plant without a permit.

The arrests come amid a series of recent saw palmetto berry cases across the Treasure Coast. Other arrests involved the alleged theft of about 200 pounds of berries in Martin County and about 150 pounds in Indian River County. In another recent case, a Boynton Beach man was arrested after deputies said they found about 500 pounds of saw palmetto berries.

hero.headline: Martin County High School evacuated after bomb threat; no evidence found
hero.body:
Martin County High School was evacuated Thursday afternoon after receiving a bomb threat via email, prompting an extensive law enforcement response and search of the campus. The Martin County Sheriff's Office found no evidence of any threat after completing a comprehensive sweep of the property.

The school notified parents and the community about the situation through social media, explaining that an increased law enforcement presence had arrived on campus in response to the emailed bomb threat received that afternoon. All students and staff were immediately evacuated from campus buildings as a precautionary measure while deputies conducted their search. The sheriff's office methodically examined the property to ensure the safety of everyone at the school.

Law enforcement completed its final sweep of Martin County High School just before 3 p.m. and determined there was no credible threat to the campus. After receiving the all-clear from the sheriff's office, students and staff were permitted to return to their classrooms. School administrators worked to resume normal operations as quickly as possible following the disruption.

Regular dismissal procedures continued as scheduled once the threat was cleared and students returned inside. The high school announced in a Facebook post that bus transportation was expected to operate without any delays. The incident caused temporary disruption to the school day but did not result in any extended closures or changes to the dismissal schedule. The sheriff's office has not released information about the origin of the email threat or whether any suspects have been identified in connection with the incident.

hero.headline: Former Fort Pierce officer charged with four felonies for tracking ex-girlfriend
hero.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield faces four felony charges after investigators say he misused police databases more than 400 times to track an ex-girlfriend over nine months. Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond.

Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith said Tuesday that Crutchfield used four different police databases to monitor a single vehicle from October 2022 to July 2023. The registered owner of the vehicle was an ex-girlfriend. According to the police report, Crutchfield conducted 382 searches using Flock cameras, which allowed him to track the victim's location and movements. Most of the queries were made when he was off duty.

"Conduct alleged in this case is unacceptable and represents a serious breach in the trust that's placed in law enforcement," Smith said. Crutchfield resigned from the department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation. Smith called the arrest "a black eye" for the department but said investigators did what had to be done.

"When there is credible evidence that an officer may have violated the law, we have an obligation to act. The badge does not provide immunity from accountability," Smith said. Smith announced changes to department policies regarding police database access, limiting who can access them and requiring permission from a deputy chief for all searches. "This is a difficult moment for our organization and our community," Smith said.

hero.headline: C-23 Canal diversion project in Martin County complete, has diverted 5 billion gallons from St. Lucie Estuary
hero.body:
The C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County is now complete and has diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water away from the Saint Lucie Estuary since beginning operational testing in May. Governor Ron DeSantis celebrated the completion Wednesday at the project site at 10297 Southwest Martin Highway, calling it part of the largest environmental restoration effort in U.S. history.

The project reroutes excess water from the C-23 Canal away from the South Fork of the Saint Lucie River, where it had previously contributed to harmful algal blooms, and sends it through a nearly 7-mile interconnect canal to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area. Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert said the project is projected to prevent 55,000 pounds of nitrogen and 14,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the Saint Lucie River on average each year and will divert 6.3 billion gallons of water annually from the river to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area.

South Florida Water Management District Executive Director Drew Bartlett said the pump station at the site is capable of moving 166 million gallons of water every day, comparable in capacity to Miami's drinking water system, and has been operational since May 14. When operating at full capacity, the pump stations can fill an Olympic-size swimming pool in just under 6 minutes.

DeSantis said his administration has invested close to $10 billion in Everglades restoration and water quality since taking office in January 2019 and has completed or broken ground on more than 90 Everglades projects. He cited reductions of 5.6 million pounds of nitrogen per year and nearly 1 million pounds of phosphorus per year as among the tangible results of those investments. Lambert pointed to measurable environmental improvements since DeSantis took office, including seagrass returning to stable levels in the Indian River Lagoon and Saint Lucie Estuary, supporting fish and manatee populations as well as the ecotourism industry. DeSantis was joined at the ribbon-cutting by Lambert, Bartlett, and South Florida Water Management District board members Chairman Goss, Ronnie Bergeron, Ben Butler, Charlotte Roman, Tom Hurley and Robert Spotswood Jr.

hero.headline: Florida ACA enrollees among nearly 1 million nationwide set to receive $500 refund checks
hero.body:
President Donald Trump announced that his administration will send $500 refund checks to nearly 1 million Americans, including Florida residents, who were overcharged for health insurance through the Affordable Care Act marketplaces. The payments stem from what Trump described as at least $500 million in excessive fees paid by consumers.

The president said the checks will be mailed to eligible people in 30 states, including Florida. Other states receiving refunds are Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Delaware, Hawaii, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming.

"Our Administration is doing the right thing and giving the money back to the people who were wrongly ripped off," Trump said in an announcement posted on social media. The checks are expected to be mailed within a few weeks.

In his announcement, Trump also called on Congress to pass his "Great Health Care Plan." The president says the proposal would lower prescription drug prices and insurance premiums while requiring greater transparency from insurers about rates and billing.

hero.headline: 85-acre entertainment district planned for Tradition in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
A nearly 85-acre entertainment district is planned for the Tradition community in Port St. Lucie along Village Parkway, and construction on the first phase could begin within six months.

Gustavo Lumer, CEO of Lumer Real Estate, is developing the Tradition Entertainment District on four parcels along Village Parkway from Innovation Way to Hegener Drive. The first phase will cover a 5.5-acre parcel off Innovation Way with 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space. Lumer said 60 percent of that space is already leased.

The full district is expected to bring around 25 new restaurants and additional stores to Tradition. The next phase will develop two parcels totaling around 60 acres farther south near the new Stars and Stripes Park. Lumer said this section would be the hub of the entertainment district and could include potentially 15 restaurants, a luxury gym, grocery stores, retail and possibly a movie theater.

Lumer said the district will be a place where people can park or arrive by golf cart and spend the afternoon visiting different venues. Neighbors in the area welcomed the development. LaVaughn Harvey said he would visit often. Tina Gramata said the district fills a community need and provides more places for people to intermingle on a regular basis.

Lumer said developers are still working on final site approvals for the first parcel off Innovation Way and will begin working on site plan approval for the remaining three sites. He said the retailers are eager to open and ready to begin operations as soon as possible.

Lumer said the development will help keep and attract business to Port St. Lucie, noting that as more brands open in the area, others realize they are missing out and will follow.

hero.headline: JetBlue ends Vero Beach-to-JFK route Sept. 9 after demand falls short
hero.body:
JetBlue permanently ended flights from Vero Beach Regional Airport to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport on Wednesday, September 9, less than a year after the route launched. The airline said demand for the route has not materialized as the company had hoped. The decision comes after the airport invested about $5 million in construction projects for baggage claim and covered walkways tied to the new JetBlue service.

JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through Boston Logan International Airport. Customers who booked flights on the JFK route were notified directly and were issued a refund to their original form of payment, according to a statement the airline provided to CBS12 in July.

JetBlue announced in December 2025 that it would begin serving Vero Beach Regional Airport with daily flights to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport and Boston Logan International Airport. The airport expected the new service to bring an influx of passengers, prompting the infrastructure improvements.

The route cancellation comes as JetBlue adds eight new nonstop routes to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport.

hero.headline: 85-acre Tradition Entertainment District moves forward in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
An 85-acre entertainment district is moving forward in the Tradition community of Port St. Lucie, with the first phase already 60 percent leased and construction expected to begin within six months. The Tradition Entertainment District will bring new restaurants and retail along Village Parkway between Innovation Way and Hegener Drive.

Gustavo Lumer, CEO of Lumer Real Estate, said the first phase will develop a 5.5-acre parcel off Innovation Way with 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space. Lumer said he plans to bring around 25 new restaurants and additional stores to the area. The retailers are eager to open, according to Lumer.

The development is divided among four parcels. The next phase will develop two parcels totaling around 60 acres farther south near the new Stars and Stripes Park. Lumer said this section would be the hub of the entertainment district, with plans for potentially 15 restaurants, a luxury gym, grocery stores, retail and possibly a movie theater. Visitors will be able to park or arrive by golf cart and spend the afternoon visiting different places, Lumer said.

Lumer said the district will help keep and attract business to Port St. Lucie. Neighbors in the area said they welcome the development. LaVaughn Harvey said he would visit often. Tina Gramata said the district fills a community need for more places where people can intermingle on a regular basis. Lumer said developers are still working on final site approvals for the first parcel off Innovation Way and will begin working on site plan approval for the remaining three sites.

hero.headline: Former Fort Pierce officer faces felony charges for tracking ex-girlfriend
hero.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield is scheduled to appear in court Wednesday on four felony charges for allegedly misusing law enforcement databases to track his ex-girlfriend. Police say Crutchfield searched his ex-girlfriend's vehicle in the department's Flock license plate reader system 382 times between October 2025 and July 2026 without a legitimate law enforcement reason. Investigators say Crutchfield also used other police databases to search for personal information.

Crutchfield was placed on administrative leave in August and later resigned from the department. He was being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on $80,000 secured bond. Fort Pierce police have tightened access to the Flock system and started a broader audit of department databases. The chief says no other violations have been found so far.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teacher uses survivor accounts to teach 9/11 to students born after attacks
cards.teaser: Ayleen Charles, a social studies teacher at Sunlight Christian Academy in Port St. Lucie, dedicates time each September to teaching students about the September 11 attacks through firsthand survivor stories and voicemails left by passengers.
cards.body:
Ayleen Charles, a social studies teacher at Sunlight Christian Academy in Port St. Lucie, makes September 11 a centerpiece of her classroom each fall. Charles, who has taught at the school for nearly a decade, uses survivor stories, images, and audio recordings to help students understand a day they never lived through.

Charles said her students have only known a world shaped by the attacks. To make the history feel real, she shares firsthand accounts from those who were there, including voicemails left by people on the airplanes. Charles said she wants to show students the realness of what happened, not just something printed in a history book.

Part of the lesson includes explaining how everyday life changed after the attacks. Charles said students are shocked when she tells them people used to be able to pass through what is now TSA security and watch airplanes take off from the gate. The lessons also cover how the nation came together after the tragedy.

Charles said the responsibility to remember will be carried forward by the students she teaches. She wants them to understand how the attacks impacted the people they know and the world they live in today. For Charles, the mission is personal. She said the people who lost their lives because of an act of hatred deserved to be remembered, and their legacy deserved to be carried on.

The new canal and pump station provide critical infrastructure for restoring water quality in the St. Lucie Estuary, which has faced water quality challenges from excess discharges.

hero.headline: C-23 diversion project in Palm City now operational, rerouting billions of gallons from St. Lucie Estuary
hero.body:
A new water management project in Palm City is redirecting billions of gallons of water away from the St. Lucie Estuary to reduce the risk of harmful algal blooms. Governor Ron DeSantis joined state environmental officials in Palm City on Wednesday to mark the completion of the C-23 Estuary Discharge Diversion Project, which entered operational testing in May and has already diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water.

The project includes nearly seven miles of new canal and a pump station that redirects excess water from the C-23 Canal to the C-44 reservoir and stormwater treatment area. Drew Bartlett, executive director of the South Florida Water Management District, said the pump station can move as much as 166 million gallons of water per day. The system has worked since May 14, according to Bartlett.

Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert said the completed project is expected to divert 6.3 billion gallons of water from the St. Lucie Estuary annually. The project is also projected to prevent an average of 55,000 pounds of nitrogen and 14,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the river each year. Historically, excess water from the C-23 Canal was routed toward the South Fork of the St. Lucie River, and those freshwater flows disrupted the estuary's natural salinity balance while carrying nutrients that contribute to algae growth.

The St. Lucie River and Indian River Lagoon suffered widespread toxic algae outbreaks in 2016 and 2018. The blooms damaged wildlife habitat, hurt local businesses and kept residents away from affected waterways. Newton Cook, who lives in Tequesta near the Indian River Lagoon, said clean water is good for the community. Cook said there has been a tremendous improvement in the water in different areas but there is still a long way to go.

The project is part of a broader network of restoration efforts involving the St. Lucie River, Indian River Lagoon and Everglades. DeSantis said Florida has committed nearly $10 billion to Everglades restoration and water quality projects since he took office in 2019. His administration has completed or begun work on more than 90 Everglades-related projects. DeSantis said a state and federal agreement is expected to accelerate completion of the Everglades Agricultural Area Reservoir south of Lake Okeechobee from 2034 to 2029. Once completed, the EAA reservoir is designed to store water from Lake Okeechobee, clean it and send it south toward the Everglades and Florida Bay rather than releasing it east into the St. Lucie River or west into the Caloosahatchee River.

cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project, citing pump capacity that can fill an Olympic pool in under six minutes and projected reductions of 55,000 pounds of nitrogen annually.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County, announcing his administration has invested close to $10 billion in Everglades restoration and water quality since taking office in January 2019. DeSantis said the nearly $10 billion figure has never been matched in state history and includes more than 90 Everglades projects completed or broken ground on during his tenure.

The project at 10297 Southwest Martin Highway will reroute excess water from the C-23 Canal away from the South Fork of the Saint Lucie River through a nearly seven-mile interconnect canal to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area. Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert said the project is projected to prevent 55,000 pounds of nitrogen and 14,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the Saint Lucie River on average each year and will divert 6.3 billion gallons of water annually. When operating at full capacity, the pump stations can fill an Olympic-size swimming pool in just under six minutes.

South Florida Water Management District Executive Director Drew Bartlett said the pump station is capable of moving 166 million gallons of water every day, comparable in capacity to Miami's drinking water system, and has been operational since May 14. Since entering its operational testing phase in May, the project has diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water away from the Saint Lucie Estuary. Lambert said seagrass has returned to stable levels in the Indian River Lagoon and Saint Lucie Estuary since DeSantis took office, supporting fish and manatee populations as well as the ecotourism industry.

DeSantis highlighted progress on the Everglades Agricultural Area reservoir south of Lake Okeechobee, which was originally scheduled for completion in 2034. Through a partnership with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers announced after President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, the project is now projected to be completed by 2029 at nearly half the original federal cost estimate. The EAA reservoir is designed to store 78 billion gallons of water and deliver 270 billion to 470 billion gallons of clean freshwater each year to the Everglades and Florida Bay. DeSantis was joined at the ribbon-cutting by Lambert, Bartlett, and South Florida Water Management District board members Chairman Goss, Ronnie Bergeron, Ben Butler, Charlotte Roman, Tom Hurley and Robert Spotswood Jr.

DeSantis was joined at the ribbon-cutting by Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert and South Florida Water Management District Executive Director Drew Bartlett, along with district board members Chairman Goss, Ronnie Bergeron, Ben Butler, Charlotte Roman, Tom Hurley and Robert Spotswood Jr. Since entering its operational testing phase in May, the project has diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water away from the Saint Lucie Estuary. DeSantis said the broader Everglades restoration effort is the largest and most ambitious restoration project in U.S. "When you think about America 250 — a massive country that spans a continent from sea to shining sea — there have been a lot of things that have been done over those 250 years, and there's never been a project of this magnitude that has been attempted, much less brought to fruition like we have," DeSantis said. cards.headline: C-23 canal diversion project in Palm City cost $57 million, took 3.5 years
cards.teaser: A ribbon-cutting in western Palm City marked the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project, which cost roughly $57 million and took about three and a half years to complete.
cards.body:
A ribbon-cutting in western Palm City marked the completion of the C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project Wednesday afternoon. The project, which cost roughly $57 million, took about three and a half years to complete.

Newton Cook, a fisherman who fishes near Jensen Beach in the Intracoastal, said the diversion will directly improve the conditions he encounters daily. "I fish near Jensen Beach in the Intracoastal, and it gets all the spoil, so it's very important to all of us who enjoy the wonders," Cook said.

Gov. Ron DeSantis was joined by the Secretary of the Florida Department of Environmental Protection and the Executive Director of the South Florida Water Management District to celebrate the milestone. The project features a nearly seven-mile canal and pump station designed to divert excess water from the C-23 Canal away from the St. Lucie Estuary and into the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area, where it will be treated before entering the estuary.

"The nearly seven miles of new canal and the pump station will provide critical infrastructure for improving water quality and helping bring the flow of the St. Lucie Estuary closer to its natural pattern," DeSantis said.

hero.headline: Former Fort Pierce officer arrested for tracking ex-girlfriend 400 times via police databases
hero.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield faces four felonies after allegedly misusing police databases more than 400 times to track an ex-girlfriend from October 2022 to July 2023. Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond.

Fort Pierce police Chief David Smith confirmed Tuesday that Crutchfield conducted 382 searches using Flock cameras and additional queries through three other police databases to monitor a single vehicle registered to his ex-girlfriend. Smith said most of the queries were made when Crutchfield was off duty.

"Conduct alleged in this case is unacceptable and represents a serious breach in the trust that's placed in law enforcement," Smith said. The police chief called the arrest a difficult moment for the department but emphasized investigators acted on their obligation when credible evidence of wrongdoing emerged. "The badge does not provide immunity from accountability," Smith said.

Crutchfield resigned from the Fort Pierce Police Department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation, according to Smith. The police chief announced the department is implementing new access restrictions for police databases, limiting who can use them and requiring permission from a deputy chief for all searches.

Smith called the arrest "a black eye" for the department but said investigators did what had to be done. "When there is credible evidence that an officer may have violated the law, we have an obligation to act," Smith said.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County advances bulk water agreement for P1 Motor Club racetrack
cards.teaser: Commissioners agreed to move forward with a bulk water service agreement for the proposed 650-acre motorsports development west of Port St. Lucie while directing staff to review utility policies over the next year.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County commissioners reached a consensus Tuesday to move forward with a bulk water service agreement for the proposed P1 Motor Club while directing staff to review the county's broader utility policies over the next year. The discussion came during the Board of County Commissioners' Sept. 8 informal meeting, where commissioners considered how the St. Lucie County Water and Sewer District should calculate water capacity for the motorsports-focused project planned on a 650-acre former citrus grove west of Port St. Lucie.

County staff said Phase 1 had been calculated at 126 equivalent residential connections, or ERCs, under the district's current methodology. P1 representatives argued the project's water demand should be lower than a traditional residential development because its garage-townhome units are intended for occasional or seasonal use. Staff said the units are built to residential standards, with kitchens and living areas, and that the district must reserve enough capacity to protect the utility system.

Commissioners agreed to pursue a bulk water agreement using the current ERC methodology to determine the project's daily water allocation. The agreement would allow P1 to manage water distribution within the project while the county retains safeguards for the utility system. The board also directed staff to begin a formal review of the county's Uniform Extension Policy and other utility-service standards, including whether bulk agreements or alternative calculation methods should be addressed for specialized developments. Staff was asked to complete that policy work within a year.

The private, members-only development is planned to include two racetracks, 125 condos and custom garages. The P1 website describes plans for more than nine miles of private track space, including a 4.5-mile P1 Circuit and a 3-mile Treasure Coast Circuit, as well as karting, rally and drift courses. The proposed development also includes trackside residences, garage townhomes, a clubhouse, event space and a motorsports-related commerce park. The site advertises its garage townhomes with full kitchens, living and dining areas, along with unlimited overnight stays for owners, families and guests.

The P1 discussion was the final major item during the nearly five-hour informal meeting. Earlier, commissioners discussed right-of-way needs and property acquisition for the estimated $30 million Selvitz Road widening project. The board asked staff to return with an update in February. Commissioners also reviewed possible changes to the use of a portion of the county's tourist development tax, received an update on efforts to address derelict vessels and long-term anchoring, and discussed potential expansions of permitted uses in agricultural zoning districts.

cards.headline: Tradition Entertainment District in Port St. Lucie moves forward with 60% of first retail phase already leased
cards.teaser: Developer Gustavo Lumer says construction on the first 40,000-square-foot parcel of the 85-acre Tradition Entertainment District could begin within six months, with 60 percent of the retail and restaurant space already leased.
cards.body:
Construction on the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District in Port St. Lucie could begin within six months, with 60 percent of the initial retail and restaurant space already leased, according to developer Gustavo Lumer.

Lumer, CEO of Lumer Real Estate, said development will start on a 5.5-acre parcel off Innovation Way that will include 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space. The nearly 85-acre entertainment district is planned along Village Parkway in the Tradition community, divided between four parcels from Innovation Way to Hegener Drive.

"The retailers are eager to open yesterday. If we could pop it up next week and have it there, they're ready to go," Lumer said.

Lumer said he hopes to bring around 25 new restaurants and additional stores to the area. The next phase will develop two parcels totaling around 60 acres farther south near the new Stars and Stripes Park. That section would serve as the hub of the entertainment district, with plans that include potentially 15 restaurants, a luxury gym, grocery stores, retail and possibly a movie theater.

"There's a need for diversity, and they keep telling us that they want different options," Lumer said.

Lumer said the district will be designed so visitors can park or arrive by golf cart and spend the afternoon moving between venues. Neighbors in the area said they welcome the development. LaVaughn Harvey said he would visit often, while neighbor Tina Gramata said the district fills a community need.

"We need more places for people to go on a regular basis to intermingle," Gramata said.

Lumer said developers are still working on final site approvals for the first parcel off Innovation Way and will begin working on site plan approval for the remaining three sites. He said the district will help keep and attract business in Port St. Lucie.

"The more brands that they keep opening, everybody's realizing, well, I'm the only one missing out, and so you'll see a lot of beautiful brands coming in a short, short time," Lumer said.

hero.body:
Former Fort Pierce police officer Josepher Crutchfield is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond after being charged with four felonies for allegedly misusing police databases to track an ex-girlfriend. Crutchfield conducted more than 400 searches from October 2022 to July 2023 to monitor a single vehicle registered to an ex-girlfriend, according to Chief Smith. Crutchfield used Flock cameras 382 times and accessed three other police databases, mostly while off duty. The Flock camera searches allowed him to track the victim's location and movements.

"Conduct alleged in this case is unacceptable and represents a serious breach in the trust that's placed in law enforcement," Smith said. Crutchfield resigned from the department in August shortly after learning he was under investigation.

Smith called the arrest "a black eye" for the department but said investigators had an obligation to act. "When there is credible evidence that an officer may have violated the law, we have an obligation to act. The badge does not provide immunity from accountability," he said.

Smith announced changes to department policies regarding police database access. The new policies limit who can access the databases and require permission from a deputy chief for all searches. "This is a difficult moment for our organization and our community," Smith said.

hero.headline: C-23 Canal diversion project in Palm City complete, diverted 5 billion gallons
hero.body:
The C-23 Canal Estuary Discharge Diversion Project in Martin County is now complete and has already diverted nearly 5 billion gallons of water away from the Saint Lucie Estuary since entering its operational testing phase in May. The project at 10297 Southwest Martin Highway reroutes excess water from the C-23 Canal through a nearly 7-mile interconnect canal to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area instead of sending it to the South Fork of the Saint Lucie River, where it had previously contributed to harmful algal blooms.

Florida Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Alexis Lambert said the project is projected to prevent 55,000 pounds of nitrogen and 14,000 pounds of phosphorus from entering the Saint Lucie River on average each year, and will divert 6.3 billion gallons of water from the river to the C-44 Reservoir and Stormwater Treatment Area. Lambert said preventing these harmful discharges will further improve the health of the estuary and the lagoon. She pointed to measurable environmental improvements including seagrass returning to stable levels in the Indian River Lagoon and Saint Lucie Estuary, supporting fish and manatee populations as well as the ecotourism industry. The Indian River Lagoon and Saint Lucie Estuary are home to more than 4,000 species of plant and wildlife.

South Florida Water Management District Executive Director Drew Bartlett said the pump station at the C-23 project site is capable of moving 166 million gallons of water every day and has been operational since May 14. When operating at full capacity, the pump stations can fill an Olympic-size swimming pool in just under 6 minutes. Bartlett said the district has not had a lost summer since Gov. Ron DeSantis took office.

DeSantis on Wednesday celebrated the completion at a ribbon-cutting ceremony, calling it part of the largest environmental restoration effort in U.S. history. He was joined by Lambert, Bartlett, and South Florida Water Management District board members Chairman Goss, Ronnie Bergeron, Ben Butler, Charlotte Roman, Tom Hurley and Robert Spotswood Jr. DeSantis said his administration has invested close to $10 billion in Everglades restoration and water quality since taking office in January 2019, a figure he said has never been matched in state history. He said his administration has completed or broken ground on more than 90 Everglades projects and cited reductions of 5.6 million pounds of nitrogen per year and nearly 1 million pounds of phosphorus per year as among the tangible results of those investments.

hero.headline: Florida Realtors puts $10 million behind Amendment 3 as opponents warn of service cuts
hero.body:
Florida Realtors is investing $10 million to promote Amendment 3, a November ballot measure that would increase the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, with inflation adjustments afterward. The measure would also lower the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead properties, including rentals and commercial buildings, from 10% to 5%.

Margy Grant, CEO of Florida Realtors, said the campaign centers on helping families afford the ongoing costs of homeownership beyond the initial purchase. "Affordability doesn't end at closing. There's lots of costs that go into homeownership. For example, insurance, repairs, property taxes," Grant said. She said the changes would help homeowners retain more of their earnings and give rental and commercial property owners more predictability.

The state's Revenue Estimating Conference projects the amendment would eventually reduce annual local, non-school property-tax revenue by about $11.8 billion if approved. The estimated losses begin at roughly $4.93 billion in fiscal year 2027–28 and grow over time. Opponents argue those losses could force cuts to services, higher fees or additional assessments. "You might pay a couple of thousand dollars less for your property taxes, but you're going to wind up paying more as the cost shifts onto fees, additional assessments," said Edie Ousley, a spokesperson for Vote No on Amendment 3.

Cities, counties and public-safety groups opposing the amendment warn the losses could force difficult choices. "Are you going to have to pay a fee to use your local library? What about fire assessment fees, storm water, additional storm water fees?" Ousley said. Grant said the impact would vary across Florida's 67 counties and expressed confidence that local officials could make decisions to manage it. Gov. Ron DeSantis has said he will help promote the amendment in some capacity, despite wanting a larger property-tax cut.

An Aug. 18 Sachs Media survey of 800 Florida voters found 63% support overall and 37% opposition. That puts support three percentage points above the 60% required for passage, within the survey's overall margin of error of plus or minus 3.5 percentage points. Voters will decide Nov. 3.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police restrict Flock camera access after stalking case
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police officers can no longer search license plates through the department's Flock camera system without approval from one of two deputy chiefs. Chief David Smith announced the new restrictions this week after former officer Josepher Crutchfield was arrested and accused of using the system to search for a woman he once dated 382 times.

Under the new rules, only lieutenants and higher-ranking officers can access the license plate reader system. Every search requires sign-off from a deputy chief and must be tied to a case number. The system can only be used to investigate forcible felonies as defined under Florida law and cases involving missing or endangered people. Camera records are now deleted after seven days instead of 30.

Before the changes, individual officers and detectives had their own user access and could search the system directly. Smith said the lieutenant-only access and deputy chief approval rules were added after the Crutchfield investigation began in August, though he had already started a one-year audit of database usage after becoming chief in February. Smith declined to give a specific date for when earlier changes took effect, saying it was roughly two months ago.

Crutchfield was arrested Tuesday on four felony counts of unauthorized computer access and was being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond. Investigators say he searched the same license plate 382 times between October 2025 and July 2026, most of the time while off duty, and that the plate belonged to a woman he had dated. He also searched for her in the FCIC, NCIC, DAVID and TLO databases, some of that going back to 2023. He resigned in August before the investigation concluded.

Smith created a new position in the department's Office of Professional Standards to conduct monthly quality assurance audits of every law enforcement database officers use. The department is also pulling cameras off the road. Smith said Fort Pierce will comply with a recent Florida Department of Transportation directive and the St. Lucie County Commission's directive covering license plate readers on state and county rights-of-way. He estimated about 50 cameras will come down, leaving roughly 20 on city roads.
hero.article_text: Fort Pierce police officers can no longer run a license plate through the department's Flock camera system on their own. That power now sits with a handful of people at the top of the department, one of several new restrictions Chief David Smith rolled out this week after a former officer was arrested and accused of using the system to search for a woman he once dated 382 times. "The cameras are here for our community's safety, not to be abused by those who were entrusted to safeguard them," Smith said. Under the new rules, every use of the license plate reader system requires sign off from one of the department's two deputy chiefs before a search is run. Only lieutenants and above can access the system at all. Every query must be tied to a case number, and the system can only be used in two situations: investigations of forcible felonies as defined under Florida law, and cases involving missing or endangered people. "The system will not be used for general investigative surveillance, intelligence gathering unrelated to an authorized investigation, or routine investigative inquiries," Smith said. See also: Argument ends in stabbing; victim flees to West Palm Beach fire station, attacked again The department is also holding onto far less of the data it collects. Smith said Flock camera records are now deleted after 7 days instead of 30. Smith laid out how the process works on the ground. If detectives at a shooting or other serious scene believe the cameras could help, the lieutenant on scene calls one of the two deputy chiefs and explains what they want to search and why. "If they receive approval, then that lieutenant would be the one to do the query for that information. And that would require a case number specifically tied to an investigation," Smith said. Before this change, individual officers and detectives had their own user access and could search the system directly. Smith also created a new position in the department's Office of Professional Standards to conduct monthly quality assurance audits of every law enforcement database officers use, not just Flock. "Accountability requires meaningful controls, supervision, and verification," Smith said. While some people who spoke to CBS12 News are happy about the changes, some say they're conflicted about Flock camera use at all. You know, we do have we do have our own rights, you know, and all this data collection and everything else is definitely infringing upon that. On the other side of it, it is a great tool for law enforcement," said Edward Smith. "I think it's a good thing that they crack down on it. Like, you don't have to have it. You know, I don't need a camera watching me walk into the bathroom." Smith said he started reviewing the department's technology policies after becoming chief in February and had already begun a one-year audit of database usage before the media brought the allegations against former officer Josepher Crutchfield to the department in August. But he said the deputy chief approval and lieutenant-only access rules were added after that investigation began. Smith declined to give a specific date for when the earlier changes took effect, saying it was roughly two months ago. "This case demonstrates that the safeguards that were in place were not sufficient," Smith said. "What we learned through this investigation reinforced the need for the changes that were already underway, and it made clear that we needed to go significantly further, and we have." Crutchfield was arrested Tuesday on four felony counts of unauthorized computer access and was being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on an $80,000 bond. Police say he searched the same license plate 382 times between October 2025 and July 2026, most of the time while off duty, and that the plate belonged to a woman he had dated. Investigators say he also searched for her in the FCIC, NCIC, DAVID and TLO databases, some of that going back to 2023. He resigned in August before the investigation concluded. When asked whether that many searches on a single plate should have raised alarms sooner, Smith said the department's audit was already working backward month by month when the media tip came in. "It's definitely unusual activity when you've got somebody doing multiple single point searches on a license plate," Smith said. "I do believe that we would have gotten there and we would have identified these." The department's broader audit is still ongoing. Smith said no additional violations have been found so far. The new rules land as Fort Pierce is also pulling cameras off the road. Smith said the department will comply with a recent Florida Department of Transportation directive and the St. Lucie County Commission's directive covering license plate readers on state and county rights-of-way. He estimated about 50 cameras will come down, leaving roughly 20 on city roads. He said the department is still working on a removal plan and it will take time. Smith defended the technology even as he restricted it, saying the cameras were integral to solving every homicide the city has closed recently and to identifying the driver in the hit-and-run that seriously injured a seven-year-old girl. I understand why people are having that discussion about the use of Flock systems. But it is an immensely useful tool to law enforcement," Smith said.

cards.headline: Former Fort Pierce officer who tracked ex with Flock cameras had 2021 sexual harassment suspension
cards.teaser: Josepher Crutchfield, arrested this week for allegedly accessing Flock and other databases 382 times to track his ex-girlfriend, was suspended for two days in 2021 after an internal affairs investigation found he sexually harassed female Fort Pierce police employees.
cards.body:
A former Fort Pierce police officer arrested this week for allegedly using law enforcement databases to track his ex-girlfriend had previously been suspended for sexually harassing female employees in 2021.

Josepher Crutchfield, who resigned from the Fort Pierce Police Department last month, was arrested Tuesday on four felony counts related to unauthorized computer access. He was being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on $80,000 secured bond. Crutchfield had previously faced an Internal Affairs investigation over allegations of sexually inappropriate behavior toward female Fort Pierce police employees in 2021. Investigators said his behavior was excessive, unwelcome, and affected the employees' work environment. The department ultimately found he violated five policies and suspended him for two days without pay.

Between October 2025 and July 2026, Crutchfield allegedly accessed the Flock database 382 times to search the same license plate, using different reason categories and without a legitimate law enforcement purpose. Most of the searches were made while he was off duty. Investigators determined the vehicle was registered to an ex-girlfriend. The investigation expanded to other databases, including FCIC, NCIC, DAVID and TLO. Investigators found Crutchfield made additional searches over the last few years to look up people's names and personal information, searches that they said had no legitimate law enforcement purpose. Those databases contain restricted personal information, including addresses and dates of birth.

The latest investigation began on Aug. 10, 2026 after the department was contacted by the media about concerns over possible misuse of its Flock automated license plate reader system. Crutchfield was placed on administrative leave on Aug. 7, 2026 and his access to law enforcement systems was revoked. A criminal investigation began and Crutchfield resigned days later on Aug. 18 before the investigation was completed. Investigators later determined there was probable cause for his arrest. Chief David Smith called the incident a black eye for the department. Fort Pierce police have tightened access to the Flock system. Only lieutenants and higher ranking officers can now use it, and each search requires approval from one of two deputy chiefs and a case number. The department also cut its data retention period from 30 days to seven days.
